name: Abigail's Flower
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Abigail's Flower is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Abigail minion. She floats towards enemies and inflicts continuous contact damage, as well as pausing to emit damaging flashes of light. When Abigail's Flower is used more than once, multiple Abigails do not spawn; instead, the existing Abigail becomes stronger and faster for each additional summon. Abigail has a visual indicator for the number of times she is summoned, with the flower on her head changing shape and hue for each stage. In Hardmode, the boost from multiple summons is much greater. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. It spawns more frequently in The Constant and Zenith worlds. Its best modifier is Fabled.

name: Acorn
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Acorn is a type of seed used to plant trees. Acorns can be planted on regular green grass, Hallowed grass, Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Jungle grass, Sand, or Snow, where they will create saplings that will grow into trees, under the right conditions. Acorns are randomly dropped when cutting down or shaking trees and can also be purchased from the Dryad for 10 Copper each. Acorns cannot be retrieved after being placed. Destroying the sapling will not yield any items. Trees grown from Acorns will be much shorter than ones naturally generated at world creation. This can be circumvented by Infused Fertilizer. Acorns can be used as ammunition for the Acorn Slingshot.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Acorn Slingshot is a weapon that uses Acorns as ammo. It fires arcing acorns that plant themselves upon landing on a suitable soil block for a tree, but otherwise bounce and roll on blocks. If the acorns reach a low enough speed without finding suitable soil or collide with an enemy, they will get destroyed and drop as items. The Acorn Slingshot has a 1/3 (33.33%) to be found as secondary loot in Living Wood Chests, and can be rarely obtained by shaking Forest, Boreal, Pearlwood and Ash trees.

name: Active Stone Block
description: The Active Stone Block and Inactive Stone Block are blocks that act as mechanisms. A given pair behave as a single block whose presence can be switched "on" or "off" using wire and a trigger. When triggered, an Active Stone Block becomes an Inactive Stone Block, and vice versa. Wires must pass through all Active/Inactive Stone Blocks that are to be triggered. An Active Stone Block is a foreground object. This means it looks and behaves as an ordinary Stone Block, inhibits movement, allows entities to stand or walk on it, blocks light, and can stop liquids. An Inactive Stone Block is a background object. While still visible, it looks like darker Stone Block, and behaves like furniture. It is essentially empty space, allowing the passage of players, items, liquids, light, etc. Inactive Stone Blocks cannot be placed next to each other without the support of other adjacent foreground blocks. Active blocks do not have this shortcoming, and switching them to Inactive afterwards using wires will still have the same outcome.

description: The Actuation Rod is a post-Skeletron, craftable tool which allows directly switching the states of Actuators without having to activate them via wire. It is compatible with Smart cursor.

name: Actuator
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Actuator is a mechanism item purchased from the Mechanic for 10 Silver each, or harvested from sand traps, lava traps, boulder traps, or Dead Man's Chest traps. It has to be placed on a tile and connected with wiring to function. When activated, the tile it is on toggles between active and inactive state, effectively allowing any block to be toggled like Active or Inactive Stone Blocks. Like Wire, Actuators are normally invisible and only become visible when a mechanism item is held. The following items interact with Actuators: They can be placed with The Grand Design (though they can also be placed by hand). They can be removed with the Wire Cutter or The Grand Design. The Presserator automatically places Actuators on objects when placing them, if the player has any. The Actuation Rod can toggle any Actuator within a limited range without requiring Wire.

name: Adamantite Ore
description: Adamantite Ore belongs to the third tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the third altar broken, either it or Titanium Ore can spawn in the cavern layer, roughly at lava depth. Mining Adamantite Ore requires a Mythril/Orichalcum Pickaxe or better. As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates. It is one of the two ores able to create Hardmode Forges, which are used for smelting all ores obtained in future progression, as well as itself.

name: Advanced Combat Techniques
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Advanced Combat Techniques is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the defense of Town NPCs by 8, their attack damage by 25%, their attack speed by 20%, and their health by 250. Advanced Combat Techniques can only be obtained by fishing during a Blood Moon. It can only be used once per world, and others cannot be fished up once one has already been used. However, multiple copies can be obtained until the first is used. The chance of fishing it up when conditions are met is 1/360 (0.28%) with 50 Fishing Power and 1/180 (0.56%) with 100 Fishing Power (assuming neither Crate Potion nor Chum Caster is used and that the body of water is not too small). When used, the status message “The book's knowledge empowers your villagers!” is displayed.

name: Aerial Bane
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Aerial Bane is a Hardmode, post-Golem bow that has a 1/4 (25%) of being dropped from Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When used, it converts any type of arrow into Aerial Bane arrows. The Aerial Bane fires a volley of six arrows per use, which travel in a sharp arc. Upon hitting an enemy, each arrow splits into five separate arrows, which are spread downwards. All arrows explode upon impact with enemies and blocks and deal 150% of the weapon's damage (64 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) against airborne enemies (i.e. enemies are considered airborne if the arrow's point of impact with them is more than 11 tiles above solid blocks). The Aerial Bane also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Unreal.

name: Alchemy Flask
description: The Alchemy Flask is a post-Skeletron crafting station used to craft potions. It has the same effect as the Alchemy Table when crafting potions: 1/3 (33.33%) chance for each ingredient not to be consumed. It is obtained by throwing an Alchemy Table into Shimmer. It fulfills a house's table requirement. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on Alchemy Flask opens its crafting menu and grants the Alchemic Enhancement buff, which increases the duration of certain buffs by 20% (see Notes for complete list). The duration increase only applies to newly received buffs; existing buffs' duration will not be changed. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon ().

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Ale Tosser is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped from the Tavernkeep. When used, it consumes and fires Ale, which is affected by gravity and shatters upon contact with an enemy or a block, damaging enemies and affecting entities in a 9×9-tile square area. It has a 1/20 (5%) chance to inflict the Confused debuff on players in PvP and enemies for 2–5 seconds, and always inflicts Tipsy debuff on players and NPCs for 1 minute 0.98 seconds. The Tipsy debuff on NPCs grants 1.1× defense, 1.1× damage, and 0.9× attack interval (about +11% attack speed). It also gains a +10% damage bonus and +5% critical strike chance bonus while the user is Tipsy, and has a 69% chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

description: The Amber Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is part of the Wizard set and is the second strongest type of gem robe, only being weaker than the Diamond Robe. The Amber Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to pierce an additional 2 enemies, and bounce up to 2 times on blocks, at the cost of dealing 80% damage. The Amber Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4, applied after the 80% damage multiplier. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Amber Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

name: Amulet of the Night

description: The Amulet of the Night is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Bat. While in bat form, the player has infinite flight and their hurt sound is replaced with a squeak. The bat form has a top movement speed of 23 mph when moving in the cardinal directions, and a top movement speed of 33 mph pixels when moving diagonally. If the player has any dashes equipped, they can also perform a dash with a special animation by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled. The player will be pulled out of the form when any of the following occurs: The player uses or places any item, including weapons. The player is submerged in liquids or is inflicted with the Wet debuff. The Amulet of the Night is dropped by Vampires during a Solar Eclipse and can be found in naturally generated chests in the Vampirism secret world seed.

name: Anchor
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Anchor is a Hardmode flail that has a 3.78% chance of being found in Pearlwood Crates, obtained from fishing. When used, it fires an Anchor in an arc, which is attached to the player via a rope. The Anchor can pierce an unlimited number of enemies in its way and returns upon hitting solid blocks or after traveling for more than 50 tiles away from the player. If it has traveled for at least 0.17 seconds, it creates a shockwave upon colliding with blocks that deals 60% of the weapon's damage (42 base damage) and 150% of its knockback (base knockback of 12 (Insane)) to enemies within a 18.75×18.75-tile square area centered on the projectile. Both the Anchor and its shockwave have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Confused debuff for 1–2 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

name: Ancient Horn
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Ancient Horn is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Basilisk Mount, which gives the player an additional jump and the ability to charge through enemies, damaging them in the process. The Ancient Horn has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Basilisks. The Basilisk mount provides accelerated land speed at 41 mph and provides increased jump height (14 tiles/28 feet), though is still hindered by water as usual. While mounted on the Basilisk, the player is immune to knockback and only takes 20% fall damage. If the Basilisk is moving at a speed of least 21 mph, running through enemies inflicts 90 base damage, not counting enemy defense. This damage is considered summon damage, meaning that minion-enhancing items will improve it. Enemies that are damaged by this attack do not inflict contact damage on the player, but the player will suffer contact damage from enemies that survive it, if the hitbox of the player gets hit. The mount emits a faint red glow from 27' underground downwards. This light does not grow stronger as the player descends, and its color is unaffected by dyes.

description: The Arkhalis is a Hardmode melee weapon that is part of Arkhalis' set and is only obtainable through Hardmode Treasure Bags in Expert Mode (except Queen Slime's). It appears to be a sword, but does not present an actual blade when used. Instead of an overhead broadsword swing or a shortsword stab, the Arkhalis autoswings and appears as a series of blurred slashes aimed in the direction of the cursor. Anything within this area takes constant damage at a rate far exceeding the weapon's stated use time. This damaging area has a rather wide spread, even attacking behind the player for a very short distance. In addition, the Arkhalis has 20 armor penetration. The Terragrim is the Arkhalis's weaker, pre-Hardmode variant that is obtainable from Enchanted Sword Shrines. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. The Arkhalis's unique means of attack is unaffected by any size and speed modifiers.

description: The Asphalt Block is a unique Hardmode block that multiplies the top speed of players running along it by 3.5×, and doubles the rate of deceleration when slowing down. It only increases the player's normal movement speed, stacking multiplicatively with buffs such as Swiftness and Well Fed, and does not directly increase acceleration. It only affects players running directly on it; the speed of enemies, NPCs, and critters will remain unaffected. Immediately after jumping or falling off of Asphalt Block, the speed will return to normal. notes:
The Asphalt Block is a unique Hardmode block that multiplies the top speed of players running along it by 3.5×, and doubles the rate of deceleration when slowing down. It only increases the player's normal movement speed, stacking multiplicatively with buffs such as Swiftness and Well Fed, and does not directly increase acceleration. It only affects players running directly on it; the speed of enemies, NPCs, and critters will remain unaffected. Immediately after jumping or falling off of Asphalt Block, the speed will return to normal.
With no other boosts, running on Asphalt gives the player a maximum running speed of 53 mph, with about 3 seconds of acceleration, while the normal maximum running speed is 15 mph.

name: Bast Statue
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Bast Statue is a furniture item that grants The Bast Defense buff to players in its vicinity, increasing their defense by 5. The buff effect can be toggled via wire. The Bast Statue can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. It can also be found as a furniture in Underground Desert Cabins. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Bast Statue, similar to Heart Lanterns and Campfires.

name: Bat Hook
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Bat Hook is a rare pre-Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook which reaches 31.25 tiles at maximum length, and has the longest reach of all pre-Hardmode hooks. The Bat Hook has a 149/22500 (0.66%) chance of being obtained from Goodie Bags. The Bat Hook has a pull-in speed of 72 mph and a hook velocity of 13.5, which makes it a very fast hook that can be acquired in the early game. However, some players may find a multi-hook (such as the Ivy Whip) preferable. The Bat Hook can be found in naturally-generated chests in the Vampirism secret world seed.

name: Bewitching Table
description: The Bewitching Table is a furniture item found naturally placed in the Dungeon and can be obtained by fishing in the Dungeon. In Hardmode, it is also sold by the Witch Doctor for 10 Gold if the Wizard is present. It emits light when placed. It fulfills a house's table requirement. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Bewitching Table grants the Bewitched buff, which increases the player's minion slots by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Bewitching Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 3×3 tiles being available.

description: The Blade of Grass is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it fires a Leaf Blade projectile that travels upwards in a circle and homes in on enemies. The Leaf Blade projectile can pass through blocks, deals 25% of the weapon's damage (4 base damage), has 20 armor penetration, and can pierce two enemies. The sword and its projectiles both have a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Poisoned debuff for 7 seconds upon hit. Its best modifier is Legendary.

name: Blade Staff
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Blade Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons an Enchanted Dagger minion. It flies towards enemies and slashes through them repeatedly at a fast pace. It also has 25 armor penetration. Enchanted Daggers arrange themselves along a carousel above the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Blade Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime. Its best modifier is generally Ballistic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 86%, the best modifier becomes Focused; if player does not use whips, the best modifier becomes Worthy. Although the Eager modifier is recognized in-game as its best modifier, the majority of enemies do not have enough defense for the extra armor penetration to provide a greater benefit, with the exception of high-defense bosses like Duke Fishron or the Empress of Light.

On enemy hits, it inflicts the Ichor debuff for 5–9 seconds and fires an ichor stream at a random angle in front of the player. name: Blinkroot
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Blinkroot is a type of herb that appears as stems with glowing dots. It grows naturally on Dirt or Mud Blocks, regardless of lighting or elevation, as long as the blocks bear no grass of any kind. Blinkroot can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Blinkroot Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Blinkroot enters and exits its bloom state randomly. Its blooming is indicated by the yellow dots and pulsating yellow light emitted. Harvesting mature Blinkroot yields 1 Blinkroot item. Harvesting blooming Blinkroot yields 1 Blinkroot item and 1–3 Blinkroot Seeds. Harvesting blooming Blinkroot with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Blinkroots and 1–5 Blinkroot Seeds instead. Both Blinkroot and Blinkroot Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

name: Blinkroot Seeds
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Blinkroot Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Blinkroots while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Blinkroots while they are fully grown. A Blinkroot plant switches between its blooming and non-blooming state at random. Its blooming state can be identified by the yellow dots on the ends of its fronds and the blinking light it emits. Each plant will drop 1–3 Blinkroot Seeds when harvested while blooming. Blinkroot Seeds can be placed on Dirt and Mud Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Blinkroots. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Underground, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

name: Blizzard in a Balloon
description: The Blizzard in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Blizzard in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10½ tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 14½ tiles, for a total height of 25 tiles. The total jump height of the Blizzard in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 19 tiles (8 + 11 from Blizzard jump) to 16 tiles (7 + 9 from Blizzard jump).

name: Blizzard in a Bottle
description: The Blizzard in a Bottle is a pre-Hardmode accessory which works similarly to the Cloud in a Bottle, allowing the player to double-jump. Instead of a cloud being produced when the player jumps, a trail of snow is produced at the player's feet. The Blizzard jump goes 8 tiles into the air, totaling 14 tiles when put together with the first jump. The Blizzard in a Bottle has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also be crafted at a Crystal Ball.

This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). It can be considered the Crimson counterpart to the Smoothie of Darkness.

name: Bloody Tear
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Bloody Tear is an event-summoning item used to summon a Blood Moon. It can only be used at night, and attempting to use it during the day or while a Blood Moon is already active will not summon a Blood Moon, affect the ongoing Blood Moon, or consume the item. The Bloody Tear has a 1/100 (1%) chance to be dropped from Blood Zombies and Dripplers, a 1/25 (4%) chance from Blood Eels, Hemogoblin Sharks, Wandering Eye Fish, and Zombie Mermen, a 1/10 (10%) chance from Clowns, and a 1/5 (20%) chance from The Bride and The Groom. The Bloody Tear can only be dropped during a Blood Moon, i.e. enemies killed after the Blood Moon has ended do not drop it. The exception to this are The Groom and The Bride, who can drop it at any time. Statue-spawned Blood Zombies and Dripplers can never drop a Bloody Tear. Additionally, Dreadnautiluses have a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance of dropping it at any time.
notes:

name: Blowgun
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Blowgun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 5 Gold. It is an indirect upgrade to the Blowpipe. When used, it fires Seeds and darts as ammunition. While a Blowgun is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds. Its best modifier is Unreal.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Bomb is an explosive that explodes 3 seconds after being thrown. The explosion breaks nearly all blocks, background walls, and furniture within a 4-tile radius, except explosion-proof objects. The explosion also deals 100 damage to all enemies, critters, and players (but not NPCs). Bombs work in liquids. The Bomb can be purchased from the Demolitionist and Skeleton Merchant for 3 Silver each or obtained from Pots, Chests, slimes, by powering Bomb Statues, or as a drop from Undead Miners with a 18/25 (72%) chance. It has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. The Hardmode variant of the Bomb is the Power Bomb. Power Bombs have a greater radius and can explode early Hardmode ores, unlike the Bomb.

name: Boulder
description: The Boulder is a unique placeable foreground object that is stationary when placed. When unsupported, it falls and begins to roll away, picking up speed and damaging players, enemies, critters, and NPCs along its path. Boulders will also begin to roll if hit with a pickaxe or drill, meaning that they cannot be picked up again once placed. Boulders will roll across flat surfaces and down slopes, but will break and disappear on contact with an obstacle. They deal 70 / 140 / 280 / 420 damage to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact, and can pierce through an unlimited number of entities. Boulders accelerate to a top speed of 27 tiles per second (36 mph) over the course of 2.17 seconds or 32 tiles. Boulder traps occur naturally in the Underground and Cavern layers, and consist of a single Boulder in the ceiling, supported by six (2×3) Active Stone Blocks wired to an Orange Pressure Plate. Once a player walks onto the Pressure Plate, the Boulder falls down and begins rolling. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, Boulders will release 2–4 miniature Boulders when they break. These function identical to the Boulder projectile, but are smaller and deal 75% damage (157 / 210 / 315). During world generation, a small number of Boulders are designated to drop a Friendly Boulder when they break. Depending on world size, 2 (small worlds), 4 (medium worlds), or 6 (large worlds) Boulders out of all the Boulders in the world are selected for this. This number is doubled in No Traps.
notes:
The Boulder is a unique placeable foreground object that is stationary when placed. When unsupported, it falls and begins to roll away, picking up speed and damaging players, enemies, critters, and NPCs along its path. Boulders will also begin to roll if hit with a pickaxe or drill, meaning that they cannot be picked up again once placed.
Boulders will roll across flat surfaces and down slopes, but will break and disappear on contact with an obstacle. They deal 70 / 140 / 280 / 420 damage to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact, and can pierce through an unlimited number of entities. Boulders accelerate to a top speed of 27 tiles per second (36 mph) over the course of 2.17 seconds or 32 tiles.
Boulder traps occur naturally in the Underground and Cavern layers, and consist of a single Boulder in the ceiling, supported by six (2×3) Active Stone Blocks wired to an Orange Pressure Plate. Once a player walks onto the Pressure Plate, the Boulder falls down and begins rolling.
In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, Boulders will release 2–4 miniature Boulders when they break. These function identical to the Boulder projectile, but are smaller and deal 75% damage (157 / 210 / 315).
During world generation, a small number of Boulders are designated to drop a Friendly Boulder when they break. Depending on world size, 2 (small worlds), 4 (medium worlds), or 6 (large worlds) Boulders out of all the Boulders in the world are selected for this. This number is doubled in No Traps.

name: Brand of the Inferno
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Brand of the Inferno is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss broadsword. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Hellfire debuff for five seconds on hit and also allows the player to "parry" incoming damage while equipped with a shield. While holding the Brand of the Inferno with any equipped shield (excluding the Huntress's Buckler), pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button will cause the player to raise the shield. When timed correctly, up to 0.33 seconds before taking a hit, the enemy's attack will be parried, which negates the contact damage being dealt to the player, deals 200% of the contact damage of the attacking enemy, inflicts a knockback value of 5 (Average), and grants the player 30 invincibility frames (60 with the Cross Necklace equipped). Successfully parrying an attack also grants the Striking Moment buff, causing the next melee-based attack to deal 500% or five times its usual base damage for the next five seconds. Alternatively, if the shield is held in place, 20 defense is temporarily gained; this lasts until the shield is lowered. The Brand of the Inferno is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Its best modifier is Legendary.

The Bug Net can be purchased from the Merchant for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 25 Silver / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1 Gold. The Lavaproof Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Golden Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are upgraded versions of the Bug Net that are bigger, swing faster, and can destroy tall grass, vines, and uproot plants just like swords and other weapons do, despite dealing no damage. They are also able to catch Underworld critters (Lavafly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Magma Snail(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)), unlike the standard Bug Net; attempting to catch one with a standard Bug Net will deal 1 damage to the player and inflict the On Fire! debuff for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 13 seconds.

name: Buggy
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Buggy is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Sluggy (more common) and Grubby (most common). Buggy is the rarest of the three. Buggy has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Buggy can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Buggy Cage). Once crafted, Buggy cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Buggy can be used as bait for fishing, with 40% bait power. Buggy can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

description: The Bundle of Balloons is an accessory that allows the wearer to perform a quadruple jump, as well as increasing the player's jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%. name: Bunny
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Bunny is a harmless critter that spawns in the Forest biome. They are the most common critters in Terraria, and are usually the first ones a new player will see. Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bunny Cage). Once crafted, the Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Bunnies can be spawned by the Bunny Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bunny to spawn in place of an ordinary one. During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile Powder/Vicious Powder, Bunnies will turn into Corrupt Bunnies or Vicious Bunnies. During the Halloween seasonal event, Bunnies spawn wearing Green Slime costumes, during Christmas, Bunnies will spawn wearing Santa costumes, and during a Party, Bunnies can spawn with Party Hats. Gem Bunnies spawn near towns in the Cavern layer.

name: Bunny Cannon
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Bunny Cannon is a Hardmode placeable furniture/weapon. It can be purchased from the Pirate for 50 Gold when the Party Girl is present and one of the mechanical bosses has been defeated. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Bunny Cannon fires an arcing Explosive Bunny projectile that bounces off blocks and pierces an infinite amount of targets. The projectile loses 50% of its momentum every time it bounces, and once it has lost most of its momentum, it will (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) transform into an Explosive Bunny critter / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) explode after several seconds. If the projectile lasts for 10 seconds without losing enough momentum, it will explode. The projectile and its explosion deal 350 classless damage and knockback of 8 (Very strong), and do not destroy blocks. The Bunny Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Bunny Cannons in the world. The angle of a placed Bunny Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Bunny Cannon to rotate it in that direction, or tapping the side of the Bunny Cannon. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, though the arcing trajectory of the Explosive Bunnies can be used to hit targets below the emplacement. Each rotation tilts the Bunny Cannon by one step (22.5°). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Bunny Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot an explosive bunny or rotate toward the side the Wire is on. When a Bunny Cannon is fired with this method, there is a cooldown of 1 minute 8 seconds before that specific Bunny Cannon can be fired again by wiring signal, and a cooldown of 7 seconds before any other Bunny Cannon in the world can be fired by wiring signal. Torches can be still used to fire Bunny Cannons during this cooldown. Explosive Bunny critters spawned by the cannon will disappear in a puff of smoke when attempting to capture it with Bug Net and deal no damage on death.

Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the bunny delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Bunny will move into an available house the next morning. Using a second Bunny License when a Town Bunny is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Bunny releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Candy Corn Rifle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that consumes Candy Corn as ammunition. When used, it rapidly fires Candy Corn shots that pierce up to two enemies and ricochet up to four times, dissipating on their fifth impact or upon hitting a third enemy. The projectiles are affected by gravity. The Candy Corn Rifle also has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%, and has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ammunition. The Candy Corn Rifle is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Candy Corn Rifle is always accompanied by 50 to 100 Candy Corn. Additional Candy Corn can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 5 CC each if the Candy Corn Rifle is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

name: Cannon
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Cannon is a Hardmode placeable furniture/weapon, purchased from the Pirate for 25 Gold. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Cannon fires an arcing Cannonball that explodes upon contact with a block. The Cannonball can also pierce through three enemies, exploding upon the fourth hit. The Cannonball and its explosion deal 300 classless damage and knockback of 8 (Very strong), and do not destroy blocks. The Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Cannons in the world. The angle of a placed Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Cannon to rotate it in that direction, or tapping the side of the Cannon. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, though the arcing trajectory of the Cannonballs can be used to hit targets below the emplacement. Each rotation tilts the Cannon by one step (22.5°). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the Wire is connected, it will either shoot a Cannonball or rotate toward the side the Wire is on. When a Cannon is fired with this method, there is a cooldown of 10 seconds before that specific Cannon can be fired again by wiring signal, and a cooldown of 2 seconds before any other Cannon in the world can be fired by wiring signal. Torches can be still used to fire Cannons during this cooldown.

Once Hardmode begins, it will no longer drop, being replaced by the Hel-Fire. On every 2nd yoyo hit, the Cascade shoots a fiery explosion towards the nearest enemy within a 13-tile radius. The Cascade and its explosion both have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 1–4 seconds. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

name: Cattiva
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Cattiva is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Cattiva minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, dealing contact damage. Additionally, it mines alongside the player with a pickaxe power equivalent to 41% (approximately that of the Iron Pickaxe) and mining speed of 16. It will continue to mine even after the player stops, as long as the player is still nearby. Cattiva will also cut down trees and cacti alongside the player, either cutting the same tree/cactus or another one nearby. It has an axe power of 171% when cutting trees and an axe power of 57% when cutting cacti, as well as a chopping speed of 16 in both cases. Only one copy of Cattiva can be summoned at a time; additional uses of the summon weapon do not summon additional minions, nor do they improve the existing minion. Like other Pals, Cattiva can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate. Cattiva has a rare chance to spawn on Grass, Jungle grass, Snow, or Ice blocks above surface during daytime if the player is not in a Graveyard biome, but it cannot spawn in the central lateral 1/4 of the world. It is initially spawned as the distressed Cattiva, with two Goblin Archers spawned around it. After killing both Goblin Archers (or making them despawn), Cattiva will turn into its item form when the player is within 6.25 tiles from it. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Its best modifier is Fabled.

name: Charged Blaster Cannon
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Charged Blaster Cannon is a Hardmode, post-Golem magic gun that has a 1/800 (0.13%) chance to drop from all basic enemies during the Martian Madness event. It possesses multiple firing modes with escalating speed, damage, and method of attack depending on how long the ⚒ Use / Attack key is held while firing it. A single tap of the ⚒ Use / Attack key fires a small energy orb that dissipates after hitting an enemy. Holding ⚒ Use / Attack rapidly fires small orbs at a rate of once every 0.17 seconds, up to a total of 6 small orbs. Mana is only consumed upon firing the first small orb. After holding ⚒ Use / Attack for 1.5 seconds (i.e., 0.67 seconds after the 6th small orb has been fired), it will shoot a larger orb with infinite piercing and 250% of the weapon's damage (250 base damage). Continuing to hold ⚒ Use / Attack fires larger orbs at a rate of once every 0.5 seconds. Mana is only consumed upon firing the first large orb. Holding ⚒ Use / Attack continuously for an additional 1.5 seconds (i.e., 0.5 seconds after the 3rd large orb has been fired) fires a large, solid blue energy beam that pierces infinitely, travels for a maximum of 150 tiles, and deals 150% of the weapon's damage (150 base damage) to enemies at a rate of every 10 ticks or six times per second. Mana is consumed at the rate of once every 0.33 seconds, i.e. 42 base mana per second. The attack is immediately canceled when mana is depleted, or when the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released, or after the beam is fired for 5 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

description: The Chlorophyte Extractinator is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses crafting station and the upgrade to the Extractinator. It has the following upgraded functions: It converts items 3.33× as fast (every 3 ticks). In Hardmode, it converts Silt, Slush, and Desert Fossils into early Hardmode ores (those that can generate from destroying altars). Existing conversions and rates are unchanged. If it is obtained in pre-Hardmode (whether via bringing it from a different world or on I am error worlds), it will not return Hardmode ores. It converts Glowing Mosses into any kind of moss (except Helium Moss), instead of only regular ones. It converts the Corruption, Crimson, and Hallow variants of most blocks into their normal variants. It converts ores and bars into their alternate ore types (such as Copper into Tin). It converts Dungeon Bricks into their variants.

name: Chlorophyte Ore
description: Chlorophyte Ore is a Hardmode ore. After Hardmode starts, Mud Blocks located near Jungle grass blocks (naturally in the Underground Jungle) in or below the bottom half of the Underground layer will occasionally be replaced by Chlorophyte Ore. It requires at least a Pickaxe Axe or Drax to be mined, whose materials require defeating all three mechanical bosses. Chlorophyte Ore is also renewable; it will slowly spread itself by converting adjacent Mud and Jungle grass blocks into more Chlorophyte Ore. It will also attempt to spread by converting nearby Dirt Blocks to Mud, as well as blocks of Corrupt, Crimson, Hallowed, and regular grass to Jungle grass. Chlorophyte Ore can only spread and convert blocks if it is in or below the bottom half of the Underground layer. It can only spread itself to directly adjacent tiles (and only if there is not too much Chlorophyte nearby already) and can only convert tiles up to six tiles away. See Technical details section for details about generation and spread of Chlorophyte Ore, and the difference of mechanics of Chlorophyte Ore in special world seeds.

name: Chromatic Cloak
description: The Chromatic Cloak is a Hardmode accessory. When equipped, touching Shimmer does not immediately inflict the Shimmering debuff, and the player can instead start Shimmering at any time by holding the ▼ Down key. However, after Shimmering starts, it cannot be interrupted, not even if the Chromatic Cloak is removed and equipped again. While the Chromatic Cloak is equipped, being submerged in Shimmer is comparable to being submerged in water: the player's horizontal and vertical movement speed are slowed by the same amount, the Shimmer can be swam in using accessories such as Flippers, and the player will transform into Merfolk if wearing the Neptune's Shell or its upgrades. However, the player cannot drown in the Shimmer; the breath meter does not appear.

name: Chum Bucket
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Chum Bucket is a consumable item that increases Fishing Power when thrown into a liquid. Chum Buckets have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped from Blood Moon enemies: Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen drop it in stacks of 4–6, and Hemogoblin Sharks, Blood Eels, and Dreadnautiluses in stacks of 7–10. All of these enemies have a chance to spawn while fishing during a Blood Moon. The Fishing Power bonus depends on how many Chum Buckets are present on the liquid's surface. A single bucket used will increase Fishing Power by 11, two for a total of 17, and finally three for a total of 20. This bonus is added after all other fishing factors; therefore, unlike other fishing gear, it is not influenced by time factors. See the relevant section on Fishing for details. Each bucket present in the pool lasts up to 10 times reeling in the line, even if nothing is on the line or if the line breaks. Reeling in the line reduces the lifetime of all Chum Buckets in the same body of liquid, rather than just one Chum Bucket. Having any Chum Buckets present on the water's surface will multiply Shark spawn rates by 5× and Orca spawn rates by 2.78×.

name: Clentaminator
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Clentaminator is a Hardmode tool which can be used to create or destroy biomes. It uses Solutions as ammunition, with each Solution spreading a different biome. It has a similar firing pattern to the Flamethrower, but has a much longer range, fires through blocks and works in water. The Clentaminator is generally the fastest means of spreading or removing Hallow, Corruption and Crimson. It can also rapidly convert Jungle to Glowing Mushroom biome and vice versa. It can be purchased from the Steampunker for 2 Platinum. After the Moon Lord is defeated, the Clentaminator can be upgraded into the Terraformer by throwing it into Shimmer. The Clentaminator cannot be purchased in Remix and Zenith worlds. The Clentaminator cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

name: Climbing Claws
description: The Climbing Claws are an accessory that lets players partially "stick" to the sides of blocks, slowly sliding down them when moving against them in midair. Jumps can also be performed off the sides of blocks. By repeatedly sticking and jumping, vertical blocks can be scaled. When sliding down, the slide speed can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Climbing Claws can be found in surface chests (including Water Chests) and they also have a 1/100 (1%) chance of being found in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates. They can also be purchased for 2 Gold 50 Silver from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waxing Crescent. Their availability very early in the game makes them a useful accessory for mobility, as they allow the player to slowly but surely climb up some walls without needing ropes. Climbing Claws function identically to the Shoe Spikes, but are found in different locations. When both Climbing Claws and Shoe Spikes are equipped, the wearer remains completely "stuck" at a fixed point when moving against the sides of blocks, and may slide down with the ▼ Down key. This effect can also be achieved using a single accessory if the Climbing Claws and Shoe Spikes are combined into the Tiger Climbing Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop.

name: Clinger Staff
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Clinger Staff is a Hardmode magic weapon that generates a 15-tile high wall of Cursed Flame, which deals damage and inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff to enemies that walk through it for a duration of 7 seconds. The point at which the wall is generated must be in a direct line of sight; otherwise, the wall will not generate, though still consume mana. The Clinger Staff's wall lasts for 5 minutes. Only one wall may be generated at a time; if another is summoned, the first one will vanish. The Clinger Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics. Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Clinger Staff's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.

description: The Clothier Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon Skeletron after it has been defeated. It has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance to drop from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon. When equipped in an accessory slot (but not social slots), the Clothier Voodoo Doll allows the player, Fallen Stars, and other NPCs to harm and kill the Clothier. Unlike the Guide Voodoo Doll, the Clothier Voodoo Doll is not destroyed upon use, and has no effect when dropped into lava. The Clothier Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

description: The Cloud in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the functionality of the Cloud in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. name: Cobweb
description: Cobwebs are crafting materials used to craft Silk and other items. Cobwebs can also be placed. Placed Cobwebs catch players who fall into them and reset fall damage. They break after a short time when a player is stuck in them, and they can also be harvested instantly with any weapon or swung tool. Cobwebs are commonly found in underground areas in clusters of 5 or more alongside the edges of walls or ceilings, and are guaranteed to drop a Cobweb item when broken. They are also found in large quantities in Spider Nests, where they regrow over time; however, Cobwebs found there only have a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop when broken. In Expert Mode worlds with the Remix seed enabled, web spit attack from Black Recluses and Jungle Creepers can randomly place Cobwebs in a 13×13 rectangular area centered on the location where Web Spit projectiles disappear.

name: Coin Gun
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Coin Gun is a Hardmode ranged weapon that uses coins as ammunition, which affects its damage and velocity depending on the type of coin fired. The weapon itself has 0 base damage, with the entirety of its damage value stemming from the coins used to fire it. Coin projectiles dissipate upon hitting an enemy or solid block and cannot be retrieved once fired. The Coin Gun is dropped very rarely (1/4000 (0.025%) chance) by regular Pirate Invasion enemies, excluding the Parrot. The Coin Gun's drop chance from Pirate Captains is quadrupled (1/1000 (0.1%) chance) and increased again from the Flying Dutchman (1/50 (2%) chance). Its best modifier is Agile, as it can only receive modifiers affecting its speed, velocity, critical strike chance, and knockback. Rapid and Hasty modifiers are recognized in-game as its "best" modifier due to them increasing the item's value by the most.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Companion Cube is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Companion Cube that follows the player. The Companion Cube can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Platinum. Normally, the Companion Cube follows the player by hopping towards them. However, when the player and the Companion Cube are in complete darkness (including the absence of light sources), the Cube can occasionally "stab" the player, inflicting 3 damage. When the Companion Cube falls into lava, it emits the Lunatic Cultist's death sound. When submerged in lava for long enough, there is a chance it may make the Moon Lord's death sound. The Companion Cube will also occasionally emit the flatulence sound normally produced by the Whoopie Cushion.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Confetti Cannon is a Hardmode novelty furniture/mechanism. It is purchased from the Party Girl for 25 Gold, when the Pirate is present. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Confetti Cannon fires a burst of multicolored gravity-affected Confetti that is purely visual, dealing no damage or knockback. The Confetti Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Confetti Cannons in the world. The angle of a placed Confetti Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Confetti Cannon to rotate it in that direction, or tapping the side of the Confetti Cannon. It has 9 possible orientations and cannot fire downward. Each step tilts the Confetti Cannon by 1/16 of a circle (22.5°). The Confetti Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot Confetti (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds) or rotate toward the side the Wire is on.

The Confetti Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Confetti Cannons in the world.
The angle of a placed Confetti Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Confetti Cannon to rotate it in that direction,  or tapping the side of the Confetti Cannon. It has 9 possible orientations and cannot fire downward. Each step tilts the Confetti Cannon by 1/16 of a circle (22.5°).
The Confetti Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot Confetti (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds) or rotate toward the side the Wire is on.

name: Constellation
description: The Constellation is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist whip. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 15 tag damage 15% tag critical strike chance Marks enemies with cosmic energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Constellation, the cosmic energy fully grows. The next time Constellation hits an enemy marked with grown cosmic energy, it releases 6 non-piercing Shooting Stars that home in on enemies after a short delay, each dealing 39.6% of the whip's damage (51 base damage) and 100% of its knockback, and the cosmic energy is reset to its non-grown state. The Shooting Stars also apply the Constellation's cosmic energy, tag damage, tag critical strike chance to enemies they hit like the whip itself, but cannot trigger the effect of grown cosmic energy and cause more Shooting Stars to spawn. All enemies hit by a swing will be marked by cosmic energy, but effect of cosmic energy can be triggered only once per swing. Uniquely among whips, the Constellation's tag effect lasts for 8 seconds instead of the usual 4 seconds. Its best modifier is Legendary.

name: Cooked Marshmallow
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Cooked Marshmallow is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Cooked Marshmallow is created by holding a Marshmallow on a Stick over a Campfire for up to 15 seconds. The Marshmallow on a Stick must be held by the player, either by attaching it to the cursor in the inventory or selecting it in the hotbar, for the entire duration over the Campfire in order for it to be cooked. Selecting a different item in the hotbar, moving/turning away from the Campfire, or turning the Campfire off resets the timer.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Corals are crafting materials which can be found in the Ocean biomes at the ends of the world. They grow naturally on Sand Blocks underwater, within 380 tiles of the left or right edges of the world, and above the depth of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) −20 feet / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 0 feet, as long as no more than 5 Corals ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Seashells) are within 7 tiles horizontally and vertically. Corals can be harvested either with a pickaxe/drill/explosives, by mining out the sand underneath them, or by placing a block above them. Afterwards, they can be placed on any type of block and will take on a random appearance out of six possible varieties. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Corals will spawn slower on sand under less than 5 tiles of water. Spawn rates scale with rain, wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Corals will only spawn on sand under at least 5 tiles of water. Rain and wind do not affect spawn rates.

name: Crimson Heart
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Crimson Heart is a background object found deep in the chasms of The Crimson. A world generated with the Crimson features several Crimson Hearts, and destroying at least three of them (in a single world) is usually a crucial step in game advancement. This can be done using any hammer or explosives. Crimson Hearts release a fair amount of their own flickering light, similar to Crimson Altars. They are the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Shadow Orbs. Crimson Hearts are usually located at the ends of the branches that split from the main circular room of the Crimson's caves, surrounded by Crimstone Blocks. In order to reach them, the player may use a Deathbringer Pickaxe or better pickaxe, explosives, or Purification Powder.

name: Crimson Rod
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Crimson Rod is a pre-Hardmode magic weapon that launches a reddish rain cloud towards the cursor, where it rains damaging blood droplets downward onto enemies below. One cloud projectile can be placed at a time and it does not pass through terrain, instead stopping if it hits a surface before it reaches its target location. Once placed, the cloud will remain for five minutes, similarly to the Nimbus Rod's cloud. As well, its coverage area is rather narrow, making it difficult to use in open areas or against agile foes. The droplets can pierce one enemy, dissipating upon hitting a second one or a solid block. The Crimson Rod has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates, which are fished in the Crimson. Its Corruption counterpart is the Vilethorn. Its best modifier is Demonic because it cannot get modifiers that affect knockback.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Crystal Ball is a Hardmode furniture item which functions as a crafting station. It is purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Crystal Ball grants the Clairvoyance buff and opens its crafting menu. The Clairvoyance buff boosts the following magic-related stats: +20 maximum mana +5% magic damage +2% magic critical strike chance −2% mana usage The Clairvoyance buff lasts until the player dies or leaves the world. The buff can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Crystal Ball must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.

description: The Crystal Serpent is a Hardmode wand that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in The Hallow biome in any layer. When used, it fires a pink charge that shatters into 3–5 smaller sparks upon impact with an enemy or block, each of which deals 80% of the weapon's damage and knockback (32 base damage and a knockback of 3.52 (Weak)). name: Crystal Shard
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Crystal Shards are a common Hardmode crafting material found in the Underground Hallow. They can naturally grow on the left, right, and bottom sides of Pearlstone, Pink Ice, Pearlsand, Hardened Pearlsand, and Pearlsandstone Blocks. Due to their constant regrowth, they can be farmed (see Guide:Farming resources § Crystal Shards for details). Crystal Shards emit a small glow, similar to Demonite Ore and Crimtane Ore. They do not spread the Hallow. When a Crystal Shard is to be grown, it has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be replaced by a Gelatin Crystal(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) instead. Crystal Shards furthermore have a 1/2 (50%) chance to be obtained from Divine Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), in stacks of 4–10. Crystal Shards are also placeable in nearly any position (on walls, floors, and ceilings), though they are often not luminous enough to replace other light sources, and placement has no other functional effect. Although natural Crystal Shards can only grow on blocks related with The Hallow, they can be placed anywhere once harvested. Crafting all items, including only one color of Phasesaber and excluding consumables and furniture, requires a total of 90 Crystal Shards. The amount required to craft every weapon and every color of Phasesaber is 290 Crystal Shards.

name: Damage Booster
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Damage Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Damage Nebula buff which immediately provides the player with a 15% damage boost for 8 seconds. When a Damage Booster is picked up while the Damage Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Damage Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Damage Booster expires, and the Damage Nebula buff decreases by one level. Damage Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.

name: Dangersense Potion
description: The Dangersense Potion is a buff potion which grants the Dangersense buff when consumed. The buff reveals hazardous traps, blocks, and objects that can potentially harm or impede the player by highlighting them in red, even in complete darkness. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Dangersense Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.

name: Daybloom
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Daybloom is a type of herb that appears as a small yellow flower with a straight green stem. It grows naturally on regular grass and Hallowed grass. Daybloom can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Daybloom Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Daybloom blooms during daytime (4:30 AM to 7:29 PM). Its blooming is indicated by the yellow sunflower-like head. Harvesting mature Daybloom yields 1 Daybloom item. Harvesting blooming Daybloom yields 1 Daybloom item and 1–3 Daybloom Seeds. Harvesting blooming Daybloom with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Dayblooms and 1–5 Daybloom Seeds instead. Both Daybloom and Daybloom Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag. Daybloom can also be dropped by Angry Dandelions.

description: Daybloom Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Dayblooms while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Dayblooms while they are fully grown. Daybloom will only bloom during daytime, showing off a sunflower-like head. Each plant will drop 1–3 Daybloom Seeds when harvested while blooming. Daybloom Seeds can be placed on pure and Hallowed grass (including Mowed grass and Mowed Hallowed grass), empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Dayblooms. They will grow anywhere, not just in direct sunlight on the Surface, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

name: Daybreak
description: The Daybreak is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist melee weapon that fires a gravity-affected sun spear projectile. It sticks onto the targeted enemy upon contact, dealing damage and inflicting the Daybroken debuff, which deals 100 damage per second for a duration of 5 seconds. Up to eight sun spears can be stuck onto a single enemy at one time, resulting in 800 DPS for the debuff. When more than eight sun spears are attached, the earliest one will dissipate and cause a Solar Explosion. Additionally, a sun spear will dissipate and cause a Solar Explosion whenever it collides with blocks, when the target it is stuck to dies, or when its duration ends. Solar Explosions deal the weapon's damage and inflicts the Daybroken debuff, but cannot deal critical hits. Its best modifier is Ruthless. Since part of the Daybreak's damage output comes from the Solar Explosions which cannot critically hit, critical hit chance bonuses are less effective than direct increases in damage.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Dead Man's Chest is a naturally-generated Chest rigged with a large variety of traps in order to kill the player upon opening it. This setup usually includes 3–5 Boulder traps, 2–6 Dart Traps, and 0–3 Explosives, with a possibility of 1–2 Geysers if generated at depths in which lava can spawn naturally. The Boulder traps are set up above the chest, the Dart Traps are set up horizontally, and the Explosives are hidden underneath. Dead Man's Chests will always generate alone, and never in an Underground Cabin. The Dead Man's Chest will contain standard Gold Chest loot based on where it is found, as well as having a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to contain the Dead Man's Sweater.

name: Deathweed Seeds
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Deathweed Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Deathweeds while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Deathweeds while they are fully grown. A Deathweed plant only blooms during Blood Moons and Full Moons. Its blooming state can be identified by the sickly red pods on its leaves. Each plant will drop 1–3 Deathweed Seeds when harvested while blooming. Deathweed Seeds can be placed on Corrupt and Crimson grass, Ebonstone and Crimstone Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Deathweeds. They will grow anywhere, not just in the evil biomes, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

name: Demon Heart
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Demon Heart is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently grants the player an extra accessory slot, for use only within Expert and Master Mode worlds. This effect does not stack and may only be used once per player. The Demon Heart is always dropped from the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. If a player opens the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag after they have already consumed a Demon Heart, another one will not be obtained. When a player who consumed a Demon Heart is in a Classic Mode world (a non-Expert or Master world), the extra accessory slot is disabled, removing all functional or display effects from any items equipped in the slot, and darkening the slot itself. Players in Classic worlds are also prevented from equipping items in the sixth or seventh slot, though an equipped item in the slot may still be taken out, and placed back into the inventory.

name: Depth Meter
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Depth Meter is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the player's vertical position, or depth. Depth is relative to the boundary between the Surface and Underground layers, which has a depth of 0 and is displayed as "Level". Depth is shown in the number of feet (1 foot = 1/2 tile) to this boundary, and is measured from the player's feet. The display also shows the name of the current layer. The Depth Meter has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Cave Bats, Jungle Bats, Ice Bats, Giant Bats, and Spore Bats. Furthermore, it has a 1/80 (1.25%) chance of being dropped from Crawdads(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Giant Shellies(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Salamanders(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

name: Desert Tiger Staff
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Desert Tiger Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Desert Tiger minion. It runs towards enemies to deal contact damage. Every six seconds, the tiger can perform a pounce attack at nearby enemies, dealing 50% extra damage (+20 base damage) and passing through blocks to reach them. When the Desert Tiger Staff is used more than once, multiple Desert Tigers do not spawn; instead, the existing Desert Tiger becomes stronger (+16/+17 damage; 40% of the weapon's listed damage, which is additive to pounce's 50%) and faster for each additional summon. The Desert Tiger appears as a cub if summoned 1 to 3 times, an adult if summoned 4 to 6 times, and an armored adult if summoned 7 or more times. The Desert Tiger Staff is always found in the Dungeon's Desert Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Desert Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach a certain threshold (including whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless. The exact threshold varies depending on the number of summons, which is listed in Notes below.

name: Detonator
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Detonators are activation Mechanisms that can be found underground as part of Traps, wired to Explosives. They are often found planted on top of suspiciously large veins of underground metals (E.g. Silver). Detonators act as switches, sending an activation trigger to other mechanisms connected to it through Wire. They are tripped either by right-clicking or when a player falls on the plunger, similar to a Pressure Plate. Unlike pressure plates, a player has to actually fall from above to trigger a detonator. Even walking off a 1.5 block high column will not work, while walking off a 2 block high column reliably triggers it. This makes explosive traps that use a detonator instead of a pressure plate slightly less dangerous as they are more difficult to trigger accidentally (as well as much easier to see). A detonator is not triggered by enemies or NPCs falling on it. When triggered by player, a detonator disables itself for one second. When activated by a wire, it is disabled until it is activated by wire again. When it is disabled, plunger is stuck down and it cannot be triggered by a player clicking it or falling on it.
notes:
Detonators are activation Mechanisms that can be found underground as part of Traps, wired to Explosives. They are often found planted on top of suspiciously large veins of underground metals (E.g. Silver).
Detonators act as switches, sending an activation trigger to other mechanisms connected to it through Wire. They are tripped either by right-clicking or when a player falls on the plunger, similar to a Pressure Plate.
Unlike pressure plates, a player has to actually fall from above to trigger a detonator. Even walking off a 1.5 block high column will not work, while walking off a 2 block high column reliably triggers it. This makes explosive traps that use a detonator instead of a pressure plate slightly less dangerous as they are more difficult to trigger accidentally (as well as much easier to see).
A detonator is not triggered by enemies or NPCs falling on it.

It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable white gemstones embedded in it, and background object form. obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Digtoise is a pre-Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Digtoise that follows the player. While holding the item, pressing ⚒ Use / Attack causes it to roll in the direction of the cursor. Upon contact with a block, it will start mining in that direction (either downwards or horizontally) 3 blocks at a time, with a pickaxe power equivalent to 26% (lower than any pickaxe) and mining speed of 20. When digging horizontally, it can pass over a one-tile gap, but a gap of two or more tiles will cause it to stop. It will also stop when it hits a block that it does not have enough pickaxe power to mine. While holding the item, pressing ⚒ Use / Attack anywhere on the screen besides Digtoise itself causes it to stop mining, while pressing ⚷ Open / Activate anywhere besides Digtoise itself causes it to despawn. Like other Pals, it can be petted by using ⚷ Open / Activate directly on it. Digtoise is rarely found as "Sleeping Digtoise", a solid object in the Underground Desert. The Sleeping Digtoise has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to replace Antlion Eggs during world generation, and has a 1/100 (1%) chance to replace Antlion Eggs when they regrow.

name: Dirt Block
description: The Dirt Block is one of the most common blocks in Terraria, occurring naturally almost everywhere throughout the world. All caves above the elevation of 0 ft are made of Dirt. Below 0 ft, in the underground layer, the caves are made of roughly 50% Dirt. Small patches of Dirt can be found in the cavern layer, though it is mostly made of Stone. Dirt Blocks may be covered by different types of grass: regular, Corrupt, Crimson, Hallowed, mowed, or mowed Hallowed. Grass spreads onto adjacent Dirt Blocks, and it can be grown manually using seeds or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth. In all cases, the grass applies to the block as a whole, and will appear on all exposed surfaces. If a grass block is covered by blocks on its four sides, the grass will remain and show as markings on the block. However, if the block is completely surrounded with eight blocks, the grass is lost and the block will revert to regular Dirt.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Dirt Rod is a unique tool that is used solely to move Dirt Blocks around, and is unlike the use of ordinary mining tools and block placement. When used while the cursor is over a Dirt Block, the block becomes a Dirt Ball projectile that sticks to the cursor as long as the ⚒ Use / Attack key is held down. The Dirt Ball can be carried through blocks and relocated anywhere on the screen. When released, the Dirt Ball is affected by gravity and also continues to carry the speed it was being moved at previously, allowing it to be "thrown". Upon impact with any blocks, a released Dirt Ball turns back into a solid Dirt Block. The Dirt Rod is purchased from the Dryad for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 Gold / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 20 Gold.

When equipped in the functional "pants" armor slot, it also provides a slow-fall effect which is exactly identical to the buff of the Featherfall Potion: negates fall damage, and reduces the player's fall speed and gravity by 2/3 (66.67%). Djinn's Curse also works with mounts and minecarts (except the Bee Mount, Djinn's Curse has no effect on it), and works during reversed gravity. Djinn's Curse has a 13/400 (3.25%) chance of being dropped by Desert Spirits.

name: Drill Containment Unit
description: The Drill Containment Unit (sometimes abbreviated to DCU) is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord mount-summoning item that summons a Drill Mount, a rideable, flying vehicle that mines tiles extremely quickly via a stream of blue lasers. It can fly and hover indefinitely and has a mining range of 15 tiles. The Drill Mount is one of the fastest controllable ways to mine in Terraria, but it has a number of special characteristics: Unlike other mounts, players cannot use any tools or weapons while riding the Drill Mount. Unlike most other mounts, players can fly through liquids while riding the Drill Mount, though they can still drown. Unlike other mining tools, the Drill Mount does not inflict damage on enemies. It also cannot mine blocks behind other blocks, rather always drilling tunnels through all blocks directly ahead of the player. Mining speed bonuses do not affect Drill Mount's mining speed. The Drill Mount flies at 41 mph vertically, 31 mph horizontally, and 51 mph diagonally. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack makes the Drill Mount mine all mineable blocks, including furniture, objects, trees, Lihzahrd Bricks, Altars (during Hardmode), and Shadow Orbs / Crimson Hearts, among others. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate makes the Drill Mount mine background walls. Holding ⚷ Open / Activate and ⚒ Use / Attack simultaneously will mine both blocks and walls. Crafting the Drill Containment Unit requires a total of 160 Luminite (thus requiring defeating the Moon Lord at least twice), 600 Chlorophyte Ore, 600 Glowing Mushrooms, 20 Ectoplasm, 120 each of Hellstone and Meteorite ores, and 40 Obsidian. This also requires four different crafting stations: a Hardmode Forge for the Chlorophyte and Spectre Bars, an Autohammer for the Shroomite Bars, an Ancient Manipulator for the Luminite Bars, and a Hardmode Anvil for the Drill Containment Unit itself.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Drippler Crippler is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Blood Eels. When thrown, it fires a thorny ball from the flail's head, which deals 50% of the weapon's damage (55 base damage). name: Drum Set
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Drum Set is a novelty furniture item used in conjunction with the Drumstick to produce drum sounds. The Drum Set and Drumstick can be purchased from the Merchant for 10 Gold and 50 Silver respectively after either the Eater of Worlds, the Brain of Cthulhu, Skeletron, or the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. To play drum sounds, the player holding the Drumstick must be standing directly over the Drum Set and press ⚒ Use / Attack. The particular drum sound played is determined by the distance from the character to the cursor. From closest to farthest, by distance from the player (approximate percentage of the screen away from the character): 0-2.5%: Kick Drum 2.5-5%: Low Tom 5-7.5%: Mid Tom 7.5-11%: Hi Tom 11-13.3%: Snare Drum 13.3-16.6%: Floor Tom 16.6-19%: Hi-Hat (closed) 19-22.5%: Hi-Hat (open) 22.5-25%: Cymbal 1 25%+: Cymbal 2
