description: The Durendal is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss whip. It has a 20% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 9 tag damage Marks enemies with enchanted energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Durendal, the hit deals 30 extra damage and a visual bright flash appears. The mark expires after its effect is triggered once, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the tag damage will still last for its usual duration. Grants the Durendal's Blessing buff, increasing whip speed by 25% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits. Its best modifier is Legendary.

name: Ebonstone Block
description: Ebonstone is a block type found in The Corruption. Before Hardmode, it is most prominent in the lining of Chasms. It requires at least a Nightmare Pickaxe or explosives to mine (this can be bypassed by using Purification Powder to turn Ebonstone to normal Stone, which is mineable with any pickaxe). Deathweed can grow on it. Ebonstone is the Corruption version of Stone (similar to Crimstone in The Crimson, or Pearlstone in The Hallow). As with Crimstone, Ebonstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Purification Powder or Green Solution used by the Clentaminator. In Hardmode, the spread of Corruption converts ordinary Stone blocks into Ebonstone. Ebonstone itself also spreads Corruption to susceptible blocks nearby.

name: Electric Eel
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Electric Eel is a Hardmode whip that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. It has a 5% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 12 tag damage 5% tag critical strike chance Inflicts its own unique debuff to enemies, causing them to take 50 damage per second. Marks enemies with electric energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Electric Eel, the hit deals 50 extra damage, plus an additional 50 damage for each enemy within a 28.125-tile radius of the marked target. The maximum damage increase is 300 with 5 or more enemies near the marked target. Additionally, when the electric energy is triggered, resonating lightning will jump from the marked target towards up to 5 nearby enemies, dealing 20 damage to them. The electric energy expires after its effect is triggered once, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the other tag effects still last for their duration. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Its best modifier is Unreal.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Elf Melter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged weapon that uses Gel for ammunition. It is an indirect upgrade to the Flamethrower. When used, it consumes one Gel and releases five bursts of fire in quick succession. The fire expands as it travels, creating a cone-like area of effect, before dissipating shortly after. The fire has 15 armor penetration, inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 20 seconds, and can pierce through three enemies. The fire's damage decreases by 15% per enemy pierced. The Elf Melter is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event with a 6.25%–16.67% / 12.5%–50% chance depending on the current wave. Its best modifier is Unreal. A modifier granting +10% speed will increase the number of flame streams per use from five to six while still consuming 1 Gel. A modifier with added velocity will increase the range of each stream, i.e. by about 5 tiles for +15% and about 3 tiles for +10%.

description: Emerald is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the standard set of items that each gem type has its own version of, and has no exclusive recipes. It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable green gemstones embedded in it, and background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Emerald gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Emerald can be found in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Emerald can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

description: The Emerald Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is part of the Wizard set and is the fourth strongest type of gem robe. The Emerald Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to stick to blocks, as well as increasing their pierce by 1. It also causes projectiles to be shot out much faster and then decelerate over time, eventually lingering in mid-air if they have not hit any blocks. The Emerald Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Emerald Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

The Emerald Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to stick to blocks, as well as increasing their pierce by 1. It also causes projectiles to be shot out much faster and then decelerate over time, eventually lingering in mid-air if they have not hit any blocks. The Emerald Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4. 
Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Emerald Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

name: Enchanted Moondial
description: The Enchanted Moondial is a Hardmode furniture item. It can be triggered by the ⚷ Open / Activate key or wires, doing so will advance time to dusk (7:30 PM) on the current or following day (depending on whether it is activated during day or night). It has a 7-day cooldown period, so once used, it will not be usable again until 7 in-game days have passed (see Notes for details). When the Enchanted Moondial is ready to be used, the dial at the top of its sprite and the moon in the middle will both glow bright blue, and the shape of the glowing moon in the middle corresponds to the current moon phase. The Enchanted Moondial is obtained by throwing an Enchanted Sundial into Shimmer. The Enchanted Moondial does not turn the time to dusk immediately. It instead "fast-forwards" time, causing it to pass 60 times faster than usual (1 hour of in-game time, which would usually take 1 minute of real-life time, takes only 1 second while the Enchanted Moondial is active). When the Enchanted Moondial is taking effect, the effect of other time-accelerating methods (beds and the Journey Mode Time Menu) will be ignored. However, unlike these methods, the Enchanted Moondial does not increase the tile update rate in the world, meaning that things like plant growth and biome spread are unaffected when it is active.

name: Enchanted Nightcrawler
description: The Enchanted Nightcrawler is a critter that appears as a glowing pink and sparkly Worm. Enchanted Nightcrawlers can spawn naturally during a Starfall when few clouds are in the sky (such as during a Lantern Night), can be obtained by crafting, and also have a 3/10 (30%) chance of being obtained from a Can Of Worms. The Enchanted Nightcrawler has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Enchanted Nightcrawler can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Enchanted Nightcrawler Cage). Once crafted, the Enchanted Nightcrawler cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Enchanted Nightcrawler can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Enchanted Pixie Dust is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Pixie. While in this form, the player will emit a dim light in a 15-block radius and gain infinite flight. Additionally, the player will be able to fit through 1-tile gaps and their hurt sound is replaced with a twinkling sound. If the player has any dashes equipped, they can also perform a dash by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled. The player loses their ability to use other items, and doing so will result in the player dismounting and returning to normal. It is dropped by Pixies with a 1/200 (0.5%) chance after defeating any mechanical boss.

description: The Enchanted Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it occasionally fires an Enchanted Beam projectile that cannot pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The Enchanted Sword can be obtained by destroying an "enchanted sword in stone" background object, which can be found in random locations underground and in Enchanted Sword Shrines. name: Enchanted Timer
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Enchanted Timer is an unobtainable accessory that periodically guarantees a critical hit. While equipped, it is automatically charged up over the course of 1.85 seconds, provided the player is standing still and is not using any items. The charge rate is halved while moving or while using an item, and doing both at once reduces the charge rate to 1/3 (33.33%). Once fully charged, the player's next attack is guaranteed to critically strike. A cooldown of 0.25 seconds follows the attack, and the Enchanted Timer begins charging up again afterwards.

name: Encumbering Stone
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Encumbering Stone is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents item pickup while inside the player's inventory. While in the inventory, the Encumbering Stone will prevent the pickup of any items, even if the player already has a stackable item in their inventory. The Encumbering Stone will also prevent items from being added to the Void Bag. Items reeled in from fishing are still placed in the player's inventory. Hearts and Stars will also be picked up even with the Encumbering Stone in the inventory. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Encumbering Stone in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Encumbering Stone and Uncumbering Stone. Toggling it to the Uncumbering Stone disables its functions, allowing the player to pick up items again. The Encumbering Stone has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being found in Sandstone Chests in the Underground Desert.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Etherian Mana is used to summon Tavernkeep's sentries during the Old One's Army event, and is dropped by all of the event's enemies. Each wave has a designated amount of mana to be dropped over its course (see wave chart), and it will be dropped in stacks of 1 by the respective number of enemies during the wave. When collected in the player's inventory, the amount of Etherian Mana they have will appear in the bottom right corner of any Tavernkeep's sentry summon weapons in the hotbar, similar to the way ammo is displayed for ranged weapons. Activating the Eternia Crystal gives the player a starting amount of 10 Etherian Mana, and each wave will produce between exactly 20, 30, or 40 Etherian Mana. Each Tavernkeep's sentry costs 10 Etherian Mana to summon, so conserving Etherian Mana and developing a strategy is key to the event. Once the Old One's Army event ends, all Etherian Mana dropped in the world and inside the player's inventory will despawn.

name: Explosive Bunny
description: The Explosive Bunny is a critter that explodes upon death. Crafting it requires a Bunny, which must be caught with any Bug Net. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Explosive Bunnies can be released as a critter, though it will always be placed at the player's feet instead of at the cursor like with most other critters. Projectiles launched by the Bunny Cannon will also release an Explosive Bunny at the projectiles position after a short period, though they cannot be caught and their explosion deals no damage to enemies or the player. The Explosive Bunny's explosion deals 350 / 700 / 1050 damage to the player (175 damage to friendly NPCs, critters, and enemies) within a 8×8-tile area centered on it, but does not destroy tiles.

Triggering Explosives cause a large explosion. The explosion destroys most placed blocks and items (except for explosion-proof items) within a radius of 10 tiles, and deals damage within a 16.25×16.25-tile area. name: Extractinator
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Extractinator (or Silt Extractinator) is a special crafting station that converts Silt, Slush, and Desert Fossils into various resources such as ores, coins, and gems. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, it can also convert Glowing Mosses into any other regular moss, fishing trash into low level bait, and other miscellaneous materials. After being placed, suitable blocks must be consumed using the ⚷ Open / Activate key directly on the Extractinator, and the converted items will be dropped. Extractable blocks are selected automatically from the player's inventory while Auto Select is activated. When an Extractinator receives a Wire signal, it will attempt to process an extractable block from a Chest placed directly next to the Extractinator. It can perform this up to once per second. It can be obtained from multiple sources, with a 4.9% chance of spawning in Frozen Chests, a 5% to 6.67% chance of spawning in Gold Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers, and a 1.86% chance of being dropped by opening Wooden Crates. Underground Cabins in the Underground Desert(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) also have a chance to contain an Extractinator as part of the random decor. Feeding blocks to the Extractinator is the only way to obtain Amber Mosquitoes, and, along with opening crates, the only reliable way to obtain a world's alternative pre-Hardmode ores.

name: Fallen Star
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Fallen Star is an item that randomly falls from the sky at night and disappears at dawn (4:30 AM). They can be used to craft Mana Crystals, which permanently increase a player's mana capacity by 20 points each. They are also used in a variety of crafting recipes, and as ammunition for the Star Cannon and Super Star Shooter. Hence, Fallen Stars can be stored in ammo slots. Fallen Stars will spawn randomly throughout the entire nighttime, and their spawn rate is determined by two factors: the world size and a multiplier randomly set at nightfall. See Notes for details. Fallen Stars emit light while on the ground, making them easy to spot at night. They cannot be placed by the player as permanent light sources, but can be combined with a Bottle to craft the Star in a Bottle. They will disappear during the day, regardless of whether they are dropped by a player, but can remain in a player's inventory or a storage item (such as a Chest) indefinitely. In the uncommon event that a Fallen Star hits an enemy or critter, it will deal 1,000 base damage to the struck entity. Fallen Stars cannot damage players, unless playing in a Remix or Zenith world. In these worlds, Fallen Stars that fall from the sky do not drop as an item on impact, and can only be obtained from pots or slimes as their bonus drop.

It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10.5 tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 18.5 tiles, for a total of 29 tiles.
Unlike most other double-jump balloons, the Fart in a Balloon's full jump is high enough for the player to take minor fall damage, unless the player has fall damage immunity accessories like the Lucky Horseshoe.

name: Featherfall Potion
description: The Featherfall Potion is a buff potion which grants the Featherfall buff when consumed. The buff negates fall damage, and reduces the player's fall speed and gravity to 1/3 (33.33%) of normal, allowing them to jump higher and fall slower. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). While the buff is active, the player can also control their falling speed more precisely depending on the Hover Controls option in gameplay settings. The three available speeds are normal gravity, the default of 1/3rd normal gravity, and 10% of normal gravity. With the default hold control scheme, the player will experience normal gravity while the ▼ Down key is held, 10% gravity while the ▲ Up key is held, and 1/3rd gravity otherwise. With the click control scheme, their gravity will be set to 1/3rd upon touching and leaving the ground, and can be increased by one stage by pressing ▼ Down or decreased by one stage by pressing ▲ Up. The Featherfall buff also works with mounts and minecarts (except for the Bee Mount), and works during reversed gravity. Fall damage will be negated even if the player is falling at normal speed or is under the effects of the Stoned debuff. In addition to being crafted, Featherfall Potions can be found in pots and chests.

name: Fertilizer
description: The Fertilizer is a consumable item which immediately grows a sapling or gemcorn into the corresponding tree. Each use causes the player character to throw out Fertilizer in a small area in front of them. If a sapling meeting the required growing conditions is present in the area of effect, it will immediately sprout into a tree of the corresponding biome, but saplings that do not meet the conditions will not sprout into trees. The Fertilizer allows saplings to grow in front of any background walls and removes the restrictions related to them, but the other growing conditions still remain. The Fertilizer will be consumed on use regardless of whether saplings grow or not.

description: Fireblossom is a type of herb which appears as a small, magma-colored flower. It grows naturally on Ash Blocks and Ash grass. Fireblossom can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Fireblossom Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Fireblossom blooms at sunset, from 3:45 PM to 7:30 PM, unless it is raining. Its blooming is indicated by the fiery flower and fire particles emitted. Harvesting mature Fireblossom yields 1 Fireblossom item. Harvesting blooming Fireblossom yields 1 Fireblossom item and 1–3 Fireblossom Seeds. Harvesting blooming Fireblossom with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Fireblossoms and 1–5 Fireblossom Seeds instead. Both Fireblossom and Fireblossom Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

description: The Firecracker is a Hardmode whip. It has a 34% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: Marks enemies with blazing energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Firecracker, a small explosion occurs and the enemy takes 2.75× the damage from the minion or sentry's attack. The explosion also hits nearby enemies for 1.75× the damage. The mark is only applied to one enemy per strike, and the explosion effect only triggers once per mark. Inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 4 seconds to all hit targets. The Firecracker has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. Its best modifier is Legendary. Light is also an option if enemies marked by the Firecracker can be attacked rapidly enough by minions or sentries.

name: Firefly
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Firefly is a harmless critter that gives off a tiny amount of light. Fireflies will spawn near grass on the surface at night, except inside houses. Their spawn rate will be randomly set everyday, making their spawn amount varying greatly each night. The Firefly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Firefly can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Firefly in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Firefly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Firefly can be used as bait for fishing, with 20% bait power. The Firefly can be spawned by the Firefly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. Its Hallow counterpart is the Lightning Bug.

name: Fireplace
description: The Fireplace is a decorative furniture item with a style similar to that of the Chimney. A Fireplace operates similarly to a Campfire, having the same dimensions, emitting light, and granting nearby players the Cozy Fire regeneration buff. The buff is applied to all players who are within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Fireplace. A Fireplace differs from a Campfire in the following ways: A Fireplace has a flat surface on which other items can be placed, and will function as a valid surface for a Placed Bottle crafting station. A Fireplace functions as a valid light source for NPC housing, while the Campfire does not. A Fireplace cannot be toggled manually via the ⚷ Open / Activate button, while the Campfire can be. However, both can be toggled via Wire. A Fireplace cannot be used to produce a Cooked Marshmallow, while a Campfire can. A Fireplace will function within water, while most Campfires (those other than the Coral Campfire, Cursed Campfire, and Ichor Campfire) will not. A Fireplace is not a crafting station.

The Fisherman's Pocket Guide can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Fisherman's Pocket Guide as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

name: Fishing Potion
description: The Fishing Potion is a buff potion which grants the Fishing buff when consumed. The buff increases Fishing Power by 15. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Fishing Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.

name: Flairon
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Flairon is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it swings like a thrown flail and releases non-piercing, homing bubbles. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the item switches it into the Flairoon. When used, it is launched like a launched flail that also releases homing bubbles while traveling. The flail retracts after contact with enemies or blocks, or after extending for more than 25 tiles. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

name: Flame Trap
description: The Flame Trap is a trap found naturally in the Jungle Temple. When activated, it fires a jet of fire, which has a maximum range of 20 ( 47) tiles, and can pierce an infinite number of targets. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3.33 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firings. The fire deals 80 / 160 / 240 damage to players (40 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 20 / 40 / 50 seconds on players (20 seconds on NPCs, enemies, and critters). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Flame Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.

name: Flamelash
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Flamelash is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand. When used, it fires a fireball that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the fireball will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the fireball homes in on nearby enemies and can pierce once, creating a small explosion upon contact with a block or second enemy. It also has a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 4–8 seconds. The Flamelash has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) obtained from Obsidian Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Hellstone Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Its best modifier is Mythical.

name: Flamethrower
description: The Flamethrower is a Hardmode, post-Skeletron Prime ranged weapon that uses Gel for ammunition. When used, it consumes one Gel and releases five bursts of fire in quick succession. The fire expands as it travels, creating a cone-like area of effect, before dissipating shortly after. The fire has 15 armor penetration, inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 20 seconds, and can pierce through three enemies. The fire's damage decreases by 15% per enemy pierced. Its best modifier is Unreal. A modifier granting +10% speed will increase the number of flame streams per use from five to six while still consuming 1 Gel. A modifier with added velocity will increase the range of each stream, i.e. by about 5 tiles for +15% and about 3 tiles for +10%.

description: The Flask of Cursed Flames is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff on hit for 3–6 seconds, which deals 24 damage per second and increases knockback on targets. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Cursed Flames cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Fledgling Wings are the only pre-Hardmode wings. Like all wings, they grant the player the ability to fly and glide when equipped, as well as not take fall damage. description: The Flint is a Hardmode melee weapon. The weapon builds up charge while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held down, and releasing the button swings it in an arc around the player, accompanied by a yellow aura that reaches further than the weapon itself and also covers behind the player. If the weapon builds up charge for at least 0.5 seconds, it begins to glow brighter and produces a charging sound, signifying that it is fully powered. Swinging the weapon in this state releases a damaging wave of fire in front of the player that quickly travels forward across the terrain. The swing deals 178% of the weapon's damage (124 base damage) regardless of its charge, while the wave of fire deals same damage as the weapon. Its best modifier is Legendary.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Flipper is an accessory that allows a player to swim in liquids. When equipped, the player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly – essentially allowing unlimited multi-jumps while within liquid. It can be found in Water Chests and Ocean/Seaside Crates.
notes: The Flipper is an accessory that allows a player to swim in liquids. When equipped, the player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly – essentially allowing unlimited multi-jumps while within liquid. It can be found in Water Chests and Ocean/Seaside Crates.

name: Flipper Potion
description: The Flipper Potion is a buff potion which grants the Flipper buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to move horizontally and vertically through water, lava, and honey without slowing down, and also allows the player to swim without equipping any swimming accessories, such as the Flipper. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Flipper Potions can be found in Pots and crates.

description: The Flying Carpet is a flight accessory that allows the player to float for 5 seconds, similar to the Hoverboard. It can be found inside Chests located within Pyramids in the Desert. It can also be obtained by throwing a Pharaoh's Robe into Shimmer. The Flying Carpet is activated by holding ↷ Jump in mid-air, after all jumps from extra jump accessories are used. Once it is activated, the player is put on an imaginary horizontal rail. Releasing the key deactivates the carpet, but it may be reactivated at a lower height if there is still flight time left.

name: Flying Knife
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Flying Knife is a Hardmode melee weapon that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it fires a controllable knife. Holding the ⚒ Use / Attack button directs the projectile's general path, although it also continuously moves on its own and ricochets off blocks. When the ⚒ Use / Attack button is released or after one minute of continuous use, the knife returns to the player. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. However, the bonus knockback granted by the Godly modifier is not always beneficial and makes it tricky to damage the same targets. For example, the knife will not necessarily be knocking enemies away from the player. Alternatively, modifiers that reduce knockback (the best being Ruthless) can be beneficial, reducing the distance enemies are knocked away from the cursor.

name: Foxparks
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Foxparks is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Foxparks minion. It does not deal contact damage, but runs and shoots fireballs towards enemies that inflict the On Fire! debuff for 5–10 seconds. When the weapon is held down using ⚒ Use / Attack, Foxparks will teleport to the player and be held while using a special flamethrower attack that does not consume any ammunition. The flamethrower attack deals 100% of Foxparks' damage (20 base damage), inflicts the On Fire! debuff for 5 seconds, can pierce through 3 targets before dissipating on the 4th hit, and loses 15% damage per hit. Only one copy of Foxparks can be summoned at a time; additional uses of the summon weapon do not summon additional minions, nor do they improve the existing minion. Like other Pals, Foxparks can be petted using ⚷ Open / Activate. Foxparks has a rare chance to spawn on Grass, Jungle grass, Snow, or Ice blocks above surface during daytime if the player is not in a Graveyard biome, but it cannot spawn in the central lateral 1/4 of the world. It is initially spawned as the distressed Foxparks, with two Goblin Archers spawned around it. After killing both Goblin Archers (or making them despawn), Foxparks will turn into its item form when the player is within 6.25 tiles from it. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades. Its best modifier is Fabled.

name: Friendly Rainbow Boulder
description: The Friendly Rainbow Boulder is a pet-summoning item obtained by throwing a Friendly Boulder into Shimmer, which summons a Rainbow Boulder pet to follow the player. When far from the player, the boulder will bounce around, leaving a rainbow trail and explosion of sparkles every bounce. This behavior appears to mimic the real Rainbow Boulder, but it will not attack enemies or locate treasure. Friendly Rainbow Boulder produces light when it bounces, meaning it is one of the only non-light pets that produces light.

name: Frog
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Frog is a harmless critter that spawns in the Jungle at any time. When in water, Frogs will swim along the water's surface. Frogs will occasionally croak when nearby. The Frog has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Frog can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Frog Cage). Once crafted, the Frog cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Frog can be spawned by the Frog Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Frog to spawn in place of an ordinary one. There is also a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to spawn a Mystic Frog(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in place of an ordinary one.

description: The Frostspark Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Lightning Boots and Ice Skates, and combines their functionality. description: The Gas Trap is a trap item obtained by throwing a Whoopie Cushion into Shimmer. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to appear in any chest when the No Traps special seed is active. After being placed in a stationary storage item, the Gas Trap will activate the next time that storage item is opened, inflicting the Poisoned debuff to all entities within a small radius, with a duration of 49 seconds / 1 minute 38 seconds / 2 minutes 3 seconds for players and 49 seconds for NPCs, enemies and critters. The Gas Trap then becomes a Used Gas Trap and can only be "refilled" by throwing it into Shimmer, producing a new Gas Trap. Only one Gas Trap will be used at a time whenever a player opens a storage item if multiple are inside. A Gas Trap will not activate if the storage item it was placed in is opened in a singleplayer world while autopause is enabled.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Gelatinous Pillion is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Winged Slime Mount. Similar to the pre-Hardmode Slime Mount, the Winged Slime offers increased jump height, provides boosted movement speed, negates fall damage, and allows continuous auto-jump by holding the ↷ Jump key. It also shares the Slime Mount's abilities to deal 40 summon damage to enemies when jumping on them from above, and floating when entering liquids. The Winged Slime Mount grants 2.66 seconds of flight time, similar to low-tier wings, allowing the player to fly up to a height of 73 tiles, as well as gliding while holding the ↷ Jump key after flight time has been exhausted. It can also hover by holding ▼ Down, similar to the Hoverboard. The Gelatinous Pillion has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime in Classic Mode, or a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Queen Slime's Treasure Bag.

name: Geyser
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Geyser is a trap that spews a vertical stream of fire which deals a base damage of 40 / 80 / 120 and a knockback of 2 (Very weak) emitting large amount of light. It will activate when a player touches it or when it is triggered via wire. Geysers are found naturally-placed in random areas that are deep enough to generate lava, including the Underworld and deeper Cavern areas. They are generated without Pressure Plates or wires attached to them. Geysers can be placed on the top or bottom of blocks, facing upward or downward respectively, but not sideways. Geysers consume no ammunition, and their output is limited only by a cooldown period of 3.33 seconds. Geyser fire streams extend up to 20 tiles up or down (which can be blocked by solid blocks) and last for 1 second. The stream also has the ability to move through solid blocks and liquids before creating the fire stream (see Notes for details).

Unlike any other spear, it is thrust in a curved motion. Upon striking an enemy, a yellow ghast projectile appears next to a random nearby enemy and flies in a straight line through it for 1 second before dissipating. name: Glow Tulip
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Glow Tulip is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Caveling Gardener that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, it flies through solid tiles while holding onto a Snare Plant in order to catch up to them. The Glow Tulip can be found rarely near the left and right edges of the world below the Surface as a plant. Depending on world size, a set amount of Glow Tulips will spawn during world generation: 2 in small worlds, 4 in medium worlds, and 6 in large worlds. Half of them are usually generated on the left side and the other half on the right side of the world. It can also be detected by the Metal Detector.

Doing so will also yield Mushroom Grass Seeds.

name: Glowing Snail
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Glowing Snail is an uncommon critter that only spawns in either surface or underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. It emits light and is quite large compared to its normal counterpart. The Glowing Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Glowing Snail can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Glowing Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Glowing Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Glowing Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 15% bait power. The Glowing Snail can be spawned by the Snail Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

description: The Glowstick is a consumable light source that can be held or tossed a fair distance. It works underwater but cannot be placed on a wall or floor like Torches can. After being thrown, a Glowstick will emit light for 5 minutes and expire afterward. Glowsticks can be purchased for 10 Copper each, either from the Merchant during the night (any moon phase) or from the Skeleton Merchant during the day (except for Full Moons). Glowsticks are always dropped from Blue, Pink, and Green Jellyfish, as well as from Flying Fish and Raincoat Zombies. They are also commonly found in Pots and Chests.

name: Gold Chest
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Gold Chest is a naturally-generated chest, with various loot as its contents. Each chest includes one special item, as well as some coins and other more common items. Gold Chests are found in Underground Cabins or randomly in the Underground and Cavern layers, as well as in the Pyramids. Apart from the initial items, Gold Chests function identically to other chests. Removing all items from a Gold Chest will allow it to be freed or broken with a pickaxe or drill. It can then be picked up, placed, and used just like any other chest, with 40 slots of storage space. There are only three minor differences to other chests: Gold Chests cannot be crafted and are only generated on world creation at the random locations; they can also be sold to an NPC at 10 Silver, which is more than the standard chest, which only sells for 1 Silver. Gold Chests have a sparkle effect when exposed to a light source, similar to coins.

It can then be picked up, placed, and used just like any other chest, with 40 slots of storage space. There are only three minor differences to other chests: Gold Chests cannot be crafted and are only generated on world creation at the random locations; they can also be sold to an NPC at 10 Silver, which is more than the standard chest, which only sells for 1 Silver. Gold Chests have a sparkle effect when exposed to a light source, similar to coins.

name: Golden Lock Box
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Golden Lock Box is a grab bag item that is always obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. It always contains one rare item normally found in locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon. It requires one Golden Key to open, which can be obtained from any Dungeon enemy, generally a Dungeon Slime. Due to the fact players will likely have several remaining keys even after unlocking every single locked chest in the Dungeon, the Lock Box can prove useful for obtaining more loot, especially if there was a Dungeon-exclusive item that did not spawn in a player's world.

name: Golden Shower
description: The Golden Shower is a Hardmode spell book that fires arcing golden ichor streams in quick succession. Each stream can hit up to 5 targets. The streams inflict the Ichor debuff for 10 seconds (15 seconds in PvP), which adds 15 armor penetration. The Golden Shower is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flames and the Hallow's Crystal Storm, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts. Its best modifier is Mythical.

name: Goldfish
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Goldfish is a critter that swims in water and walks on land during rain. It flops in place when out of water and rain; it does not take damage while doing so. The Goldfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Goldfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fish Bowl). Once crafted, the Goldfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Goldfish can be spawned by the Fish Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Goldfish to spawn in place of an ordinary one. During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile Powder/Vicious Powder(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Goldfish will turn into Corrupt Goldfish or Vicious Goldfish(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Golem Fist is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires a large, high-velocity fist attached to a chain that retracts on impact with enemies or blocks, or after traveling for more than 31.25 tiles away from the player.. Upon hitting enemies or blocks, it creates a shockwave that deals 100% of the weapon's damage and knockback to nearby enemies if extended by more than 9.375 tiles. Both the Golem Fist and its shockwave have a 1/3 (33.33%) to inflict the Confused debuff for 1-2 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

description: The Grass Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in above-ground tunnels and grottoes on the surface, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

name: Grasshopper
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Grasshopper is a type of critter that can be found when destroying grass plants and moves by hopping along the ground identically to slimes. The Grasshopper has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Grasshopper can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grasshopper Cage). Once crafted, the Grasshopper cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Grasshopper can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power. The Grasshopper can be spawned by the Grasshopper Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Grasshopper to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

name: Grate
description: The Grate is a foreground block which allows liquids to fall through while remaining solid for everything else, acting like a drainage system. Grates can be toggled open and closed when triggered via wire. An open Grate is transparent, allowing light and liquid through, while a closed Grate is opaque and acts as a solid block. If a Grate is triggered while liquid is passing through it, the Grate holds the liquid until it is opened again or the liquid is removed by a player, e.g. via the use of an Empty Bucket, Super Absorbant Sponge, or Dry Bomb. Bubbles function as the opposite of Grates, acting as background objects which prevent the flow of liquids through them but allow through other things like players. Grates are not destroyed when dropped in lava, despite having a rarity of .

name: Graveyard
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Graveyard is a mini-biome that starts to appear when at least five Tombstones are near the player and completes when at least seven Tombstones are near the player. Some special visual effects can be seen in the Graveyard, and these effects grow stronger as more Tombstones are added, capped at nine Tombstones: colors desaturate, lightning randomly strikes in the background, and Ecto Mist accumulates on the ground. When at least seven Tombstones are nearby, the Graveyard biome will gain additional functional effects: unique Graveyard enemies spawn here day and night, as well as the usual creatures originally spawning at night. The spawn rate is not increased, but the enemy spawn reduction of towns is weakened. NPC vendors have unique trades here, and the Ecto Mist on the ground enables unique crafting recipes for the player. Sunflowers can prevent the forming of Graveyards: each Sunflower nearby negates the presence of one Tombstone.

name: Gravitation Potion
description: The Gravitation Potion is a buff potion which grants the Gravitation buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to invert gravity with ▲ Up, making the screen appear upside-down and causing the player to fall upwards and walk on top of ceilings. The effect can be toggled while in midair. This lasts for 3 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Gravitation Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.

name: Gray Zapinator
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Gray Zapinator is a pre-Hardmode-exclusive magic gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 17 Gold. It is only available once King Slime, the Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds, Brain of Cthulhu, Queen Bee, Deerclops, or Skeletron has been defeated. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Orange Zapinator. The weapon fires a blue laser beam that behaves very erratically. Upon striking an enemy, the projectile slows down by 40%, decreases its current damage and knockback by 10%, and can choose from an assortment of special effects as described below. The laser beam will disappear after hitting eight enemies or after 60 seconds. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, it costs no mana to use. Its best modifier is Mythical.

description: The Greater Healing Potion is a Hardmode recovery potion that restores 150 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. Greater Healing Potions can be crafted using materials found in The Hallow or obtained from most Hardmode bosses as well as from Biome Mimics and Martian Saucers. It is the third tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion and Healing Potion, and preceding the Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion.

name: Grenade Launcher
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Grenade Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher. When used, it consumes rockets and launches grenades that explode after three seconds have passed or upon contact with enemies. The grenades are strongly affected by gravity and can damage the player for a flat 60 damage. The Grenade Launcher has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to be dropped from Plantera, and it is guaranteed to drop the first time Plantera is defeated (unless in Expert Mode, where she drops her Treasure Bag instead). In addition, 50–149 Rocket Is will be dropped alongside the Grenade Launcher. Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.

name: Grubby
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Grubby is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Sluggy (rarer) and Buggy (rarest). Grubby is the most common of the three. Grubby has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Grubby can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grubby Cage). Once crafted, Grubby cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Grubby can be used as bait for fishing, with 15% bait power. Grubby can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

name: Guide Voodoo Doll
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Guide Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon the Wall of Flesh. It is a guaranteed drop from Voodoo Demons, a fairly rare enemy in the Underworld. If the item is dropped and destroyed by lava in the Underworld, the Guide will instantly die and the Wall of Flesh will be summoned. The Guide must be alive for this process to occur. If the item is destroyed by lava elsewhere, the Guide will die as normal but the boss will not be summoned; if the item is destroyed by lava when the Guide is not alive, the item will be wasted without summoning the boss. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, if more than one Guide Voodoo Doll is in a stack upon being destroyed by lava, other NPCs will be killed alongside the Guide depending on the amount within the stack. However, the Wall of Flesh will only be summoned once. When the Guide Voodoo Doll is equipped as an accessory, it becomes possible for the player and other NPCs to kill the Guide with direct attacks from weapons (which normally would not damage him). The Guide Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

description: The Ham Bat is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Pigrons. It gains slightly increased damage if a food buff is active. Killing an enemy with the Ham Bat grants the Hearty Meal buff, which increases the player's health regeneration by 3 per second. This lasts for 7 seconds, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). name: Harp
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Harp is a Hardmode crafting material, used only to craft the Magical Harp. While the Harp can be used itself, it has no functional use, and only makes sounds. It is sold by the Wizard for 1 Gold each. When used, the Harp generates harp sounds. The sound's pitch is determined by the distance between the center of the character and the point clicked. Clicking the center of the character plays middle C, while clicking at a distance of at least that of the top or bottom of the screen plays C6 (two octaves above middle C). The smallest interval between notes the harp can play is a whole tone, or two semitones. A difference of 1/24 of the screen height equals an interval of a whole tone.

name: Harpoon
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Harpoon is a unique pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that auto-fires an arcing spear projectile connected to the player via a chain that pierces through enemies and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 8–12 seconds on hit. It retracts if it hits a third enemy, collides with solid blocks, has traveled for more than 62.5 tiles away from the player, or if the player lets go of the ⚒ Use / Attack button. Its physics are similar to launched flails, though it is highly affected by gravity. The Harpoon has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by most enemies during a Goblin Army. The Harpoon only has an attack cooldown of 0.08 seconds after its spear is fully retracted; meaning its fire rate is mostly dependent only on how long it takes for it to retract. The projectile also pierces infinitely and goes through blocks on its return trip, similar to a flail or boomerang, making it effective for crowd control. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

name: Hat Rack
description: The Hat Rack is a decorative furniture item that can be used to display up to two helmet-slot armor and vanity items, as well as dyes. Items can be placed on a Hat Rack by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are two slots for two helmets, in addition to an associated dye slot underneath each one. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Hat Rack. Items placed in the left slot are displayed on the upper part of the Hat Rack, while items placed in the right slot are displayed on the lower part. Items cannot be displayed on the middle, top part.

name: Healing Potion
description: The Healing Potion is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that restores 100 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It is the second tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion and preceding the Greater Healing Potion, Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion. In addition to being crafted, Healing Potions can be found naturally in pots during Hardmode and pots in the Underworld in pre-Hardmode. Healing Potions are also dropped by Deerclops, Skeletron, and the Wall of Flesh, and are sold by the Merchant and the Skeleton Merchant in Hardmode for 10 Silver.

name: Heart
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Hearts (or Candy Apples during Halloween and Candy Canes during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by slain enemies, broken pots, or as a bonus drop from slimes. Enemies and pots will only drop Hearts when the closest player does not have full health. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed and restore 20 health. They emit a faint red light. If the player does not have full health but has full mana, the chance of an enemy dropping a Heart is 1/12 (8.33%). If the player also does not have full mana, then this chance becomes 1/24 (4.17%), as Hearts and Stars cannot be dropped at the same time. See Notes for more details. For the Heart drop chance from pots, see Pot § Upon breaking. It is also possible to spawn Hearts (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Heart Statue. Hearts can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Heartreach Potion to 18.25 tiles.

name: Heartreach Potion
description: The Heartreach Potion is a buff potion which grants the Heartreach buff when consumed. The buff increases the pickup range of life recovery Hearts by 15.625 tiles, from 2.625 tiles to a total of 18.25 tiles. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Heartreach Potions can be found in Pots and crates.

name: Hellforge
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Hellforge is a crafting station that functions as a regular Furnace, with the additional ability of smelting Hellstone into Hellstone Bars. It is also used to craft the essential Adamantite/Titanium Forge in Hardmode. Like its predecessor, it emits light when placed and is not a valid light source for housing. The Hellforge cannot be crafted, and is instead found in Ruined Houses in the Underworld or obtained from Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates. It can only be collected from the Underworld with tools with at least 65% pickaxe power, i.e. a Deathbringer/Nightmare Pickaxe or better is required. It cannot be broken by explosives during pre-Hardmode.

Hellstone releases a half-tile of lava when mined in The Underworld. Hellstone inflicts the Burning debuff on players who touch it, which can be negated through items such as the Obsidian Skull and Obsidian Skin Potion.

name: Hellstone Bar
description: The Hellstone Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. It is used to craft some of the most powerful equipment available pre-Hardmode, and remains useful, if not necessary, in dealing with the shift in difficulty upon entering Hardmode. Notably, the Molten Pickaxe is the only pre-Hardmode pickaxe capable of mining the first tier of Hardmode ores, Cobalt and Palladium.

name: Hellstone Brick
description: Hellstone Bricks are placeable blocks that occur naturally in unique Ruined Houses, though they can also be crafted. Like plain Hellstone, players without an Obsidian Skull or one of its upgrades in their accessory slot will receive the Burning debuff from making contact with the brick. Mining the block or carrying it in one's inventory incurs no negative effect, however. As with most damaging blocks, NPCs and enemies are immune to this damage. Unlike Hellstone itself, Hellstone Bricks are always vulnerable to explosions.

name: Herb Bag
description: The Herb Bag is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains 2–40 herbs and/or herb seeds. Herb Bags can be found in Chests on the surface. A Herb Bag contains 2–5 stacks of 2–8 items each, determined randomly when opened (see Notes for details). It is possible that some or all stacks are of the same item, in which case the stacks are merged. Therefore, Herb Bags always contain at least one and at most five different items.

name: High Test Fishing Line
description: The High Test Fishing Line is an accessory that prevents fishing line from breaking while fishing when equipped. Without the High Test Fishing Line equipped, there is a 1/7 (14.29%) chance that the line will break on any reel-in that was supposed to yield a catch. The High Test Fishing Line can be acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a High Test Fishing Line as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 High Velocity Bullets is 9 Silver 50 Copper, which is 19 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 High Velocity Bullets is 19 Gold.

name: Hive
description: Hive is a block type that Bee Hives are made from. Upon mining it may either turn into liquid honey, spawn in a Bee, or simply drop like a regular item. Hive blocks can also be acquired by dropping Honey Blocks or Crispy Honey Blocks into Shimmer. Hive blocks can only be placed using a Hive Wand, consuming Hive blocks from the player's inventory. While using the Hive block directly, there is a 1/30 (3.33%) chance per tick (average of once every 0.5 seconds) to release a bee projectile that chases enemies, without consuming the item. The bee projectile deals 5 base damage and is considered a melee projectile, meaning it can critically strike using the player's melee critical strike chance, and benefit from melee effects such as Flasks, Magma Stone, Frost armor's set bonus, and Sharpening Station, but does not have its damage boosted by the player's melee damage bonuses. Hive blocks can be converted into Honey Blocks when used on an Extractinator.

name: Honeyed Goggles
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Honeyed Goggles is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bee Mount which grants limited flight. The Honeyed Goggles have a 1/20 (5%) / 11/100 (11%) chance of being dropped from the Queen Bee. While the Bee Mount is slow on the ground, it is capable of flying and will greatly increase in speed while doing so. While flying, the player's vertical speed is kept constant. The Bee Mount can fly in the air for 10.66 seconds before it enters a "tired" state, during which it slows and glides down. The glide can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Afterwards, it requires a 3-second rest period on the ground in order to begin flying at full speed again. If the player takes off again immediately after landing an exhausted bee, it will fly, but much slower than usual. Its rest period is indicated by a "heavy breathing" animation that stops when the Bee Mount has fully recovered.

This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It can also be used to craft Seafood Dinners. The Honeyfin can only be fished from honey, e.g. in Bee Hives within the Underground Jungle. Other than the Bumblebee Tuna that can be found during Angler quests, Honeyfins are the only fish that can be caught in honey.

description: The Ice Rod is a Hardmode magic weapon that autofires blocks of ice, which have the unique ability of placing solid, temporary Ice Blocks at the location of the cursor and which last for 15 seconds before shattering. These Ice Blocks are translucent, cast a dim, flickering blue light, and are slippery like normal Ice Blocks. The Ice Rod can be purchased from the Wizard for 50 GC. The location of the cursor must be unoccupied in order to form an Ice Block. If the tile is occupied either by blocks or background objects, the fired Ice Block acts as an ordinary projectile, flying in a straight line and unaffected by gravity, and shatters when it hits an enemy or other foreground objects. If the cursor is on an existing Ice Block from a previous casting, it will cause the next projectile to pass through the existing Ice Block. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Ice Skates have a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

name: Inferno Potion
description: The Inferno Potion is a buff potion that grants the Inferno buff when consumed. The buff casts a spinning ring of fire around the player that deals 20 damage per second and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 2 seconds to all enemies inside of it while also giving off light. Critters and other passive NPCs are unaffected. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Inferno Potions can be found in Shadow Chests.

name: Infused Fertilizer
description: The Infused Fertilizer is a consumable item which immediately grows a sapling or gemcorn into extra-tall versions of their respective trees, similar to the Fertilizer. It is obtained by throwing Fertilizer into Shimmer. Similar to Fertilizer, for Infused Fertilizer to work, the sapling must fulfill the growing requirements (besides the restrictions related to background walls behind the sapling, which will be ignored), but needs higher vertical clearance, unlike Fertilizer: 29–40 tiles for Mahogany trees, 35–39 tiles for Palm trees, 26–31 tiles for gem trees, and 24–35 tiles for all other types of trees. Saplings that do not fulfill the growing requirements will not sprout into trees but still consume the Infused Fertilizer.

name: Invisibility Potion
description: The Invisibility Potion is a buff potion that grants the Invisibility buff when consumed. This lasts for 3 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). The buff is furthermore immediately canceled if the player takes damage of any kind. The buff provides the following effects: The player becomes invisible, including their armor, vanity items, and mount. −17% enemy spawn rates and −20% maximum enemy spawn count. −750 aggro, meaning enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details). This does not prevent enemies from firing projectiles at the player. Attacking or using any item will cause the player to reappear temporarily and reduce the aggro reduction bonus to –250. In addition to being crafted, Invisibility Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.

The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Joja Cola is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 2 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). It has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being fished up instead of a junk item when fishing. When talking to the Dryad and holding a Joja Cola, the Dryad's “Status” option will be replaced by “Purify”. Upon selecting this option, the Dryad will summon a star-shaped portal with a Junimo pet jumping out of it after a brief delay. The pet will pull a Stardrop from the ground and then vanish, dropping the item for the player to collect. This process can be repeated an unlimited number of times.

description: The Jousting Lance is a Hardmode melee weapon purchased from the Zoologist for 6 Gold after filling out 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary. When attacking using ⚒ Use / Attack, the lance will extend, and holding ⚒ Use / Attack will keep it extended at a fixed angle. The damage and knockback will increase depending on the player's movement speed, making mounts, sprinting accessories, or dash abilities (such as those granted by Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi/Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor) useful for maximizing damage. When the player takes damage, the Jousting Lance will stop being active. It is the precursor to the Hallowed and Shadow Jousting Lances. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Jungle Turtle is a harmless critter that spawns in or near a body of water on the surface Jungle at any time. Like its Forest counterpart, it moves slowly on land and swims at the surface of water. The Jungle Turtle has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Jungle Turtle can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Jungle Turtle Cage). Once crafted, the Jungle Turtle cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Jungle Turtle can be spawned by the Turtle Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

description: The Keybrand is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 399/40,000 (0.9975%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Hell Armored Bones, and Rusty Armored Bones in the Hardmode Dungeon. It deals increased damage against enemies depending on their missing health, up to a maximum of 200% damage against enemies that have less than 10% health remaining. The Keybrand also has a 20% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapon, causing it to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds, or touching any solid block, then embed itself in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches it. It can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. It can also be recalled mid-throw. Its best modifier is Legendary.

name: Killing Deck
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Killing Deck is a Hardmode magic weapon that can be purchased from the Wizard for 20 GC during a Blood Moon. It launches Killing Card projectiles that fly for 0.5 seconds in a serpentine pattern before abruptly falling. They stick to any block or enemy they hit, but stop dealing damage after becoming stuck, and return to the player 5 seconds after the impact. While returning, the cards fly in a straight line and can travel through blocks, deal 150% of the weapon's damage (33 base damage), and pierce infinitely. The Killing Deck cycles through four attacks, advancing to the next one on each use of the weapon: Launches a single Killing Card projectile in the direction of the cursor. Launches one Killing Card in the direction of the cursor and another one in the opposite direction. Launches a spread of six Killing Cards. Recalls all Killing Cards immediately, causing them to return to the player early. If no cards are out anymore when this attack is used, then it is skipped and the first attack is used again instead. Its best modifier is Mythical.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Ladybug is a small uncommon critter that can be found in Forests with a town during the Windy Day event at daytime. The Ladybug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Ladybug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Ladybug Cage). Once crafted, the Ladybug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Ladybug can be used as bait for fishing, with 17% bait power. There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Ladybug to spawn in place of an ordinary one. Touching naturally spawned Ladybugs will temporarily increase the player's luck, while killing natural or player-released Ladybugs or consuming them as bait will temporarily decrease the player's luck and boost the chance of rain. See Luck#Detailed Ladybug luck for a detailed explanation. However, using them for crafting does not affect luck, allowing the following recipes to be made consequence-free.

name: Last Prism
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Last Prism is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord magic weapon that fires several colored beams of light that converge into one focused beam as it charges, dealing massive damage. It has one of the highest base DPS in the game at the cost of rapidly consuming mana. The Last Prism has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. The Last Prism projects six rainbow-colored beams that deal individual damage as they begin to rotate, then spin faster as they converge into one concentrated beam. This process takes exactly 3.365 seconds, with each beam continuing to deal the weapon's full base damage. The fully-converged beam deals three times the weapon's base damage, or 300 damage per hit. Unlike most piercing attacks, the weapon hits 12 times per second (every 5 game ticks). The mana cost will increase exponentially as the beam converges. Due to its high mana cost (144 mana per second; 12 mana 12 times per second when fully charged), players will struggle to maintain the beam for more than 5–6 seconds. Usage of the Mana Flower, Magic Cuffs, Nebula armor, and a large supply of Super Mana Potions with the Last Prism is recommended. Its best modifier is Mythical or Masterful. The Last Prism is unaffected by attack speed bonuses, meaning that Mythical provides +5% critical strike chance while Masterful lowers the weapon's mana cost.

name: Lava Charm
description: The Lava Charm is an accessory that grants immunity to lava for 7 seconds. It is found in Chests located in the cavern layer as well as obtained from Hellstone Crates and Obsidian Crates with a 1/20 (5%) chance. It can only be found in Chests in the lower portion of the Caverns where lava pools can naturally spawn, as opposed to Chests throughout the entirety of the Caverns. When the Lava Charm is equipped and the player comes into contact with lava, a 7-second countdown begins, signified by a lava meter that displays over the player's head. It operates similarly to the breath meter, but displays flame icons instead of bubbles. Lava immunity time is recharged gradually by exiting lava, the same way breathing time is recharged by exiting water (albeit much more slowly).

name: Lava Waders
description: The Lava Waders are a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to stand and walk on the surface of all liquids. When walking on liquid, press the ▼ Down key allows submerging into the liquid. Prevents fall damage when landing on the surface of any liquid. Immunity to the Burning debuff. Immunity to lava for 7 seconds. Decreases the damage taken from lava from 80 to 35, and reduces the duration of On Fire! debuff inflicted by lava from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds. Equipping the Ash Wood armor at the same time provides immunity to lava damage and debuff.

name: Lavafly
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Lavafly is a critter that spawns occasionally in the Underworld at night. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld at any time. Also from destroyed wild Ash grass plants at any time and even outside of the Underworld.It gives off a tiny amount of light, similarly to the Firefly. The Lavafly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Lavafly can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net or the Golden Bug Net. Trying to catch it with a standard Bug Net will only set the player on fire. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Lavafly in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Lavafly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Lavafly can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power. Using it as bait also allows fishing in lava.

name: Lesser Healing Potion
description: The Lesser Healing Potion is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that restores 50 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It is the first tier of healing potion, preceding the Healing Potion, Greater Healing Potion, Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion. In addition to being crafted, Lesser Healing Potions can also be found naturally in pots (only in pre-Hardmode), generated chests, Wooden and Pearlwood Crates, or dropped from most early pre-Hardmode bosses. They can also be purchased for 3 Silver from the Merchant, or from the Skeleton Merchant during moon phases 2, 4, 6, and 8: . Naturally-placed Lesser Healing Potions appear frequently on platforms in the Dungeon (along with Lesser Mana Potions). When encountered in placed form, they function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. They also show the "bottle" tooltip on the map. They can be freed with a pickaxe or ⚷ Open / Activate and retrieved, and can be placed by the player by crafting them into Decorative Healing Potions.

The Lever can be placed on any flat surface, the same as furniture, including on platforms. It can also be placed on background walls. Despite its depiction as a switch with two positions, the Lever does not need to act as an on/off mechanism. When wired to Dart Traps, for example, activating the Lever will always cause the trap to shoot, the same as a Pressure Plate would, no matter which position the Lever happens to be in.
