name: Life Booster
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Life Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Life Nebula buff which immediately increases the player's health regeneration rate by 3 health per second for 8 seconds. When a Life Booster is picked up while the Life Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Life Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Life Booster expires, and the Life Nebula buff decreases by one level. All levels of Life Booster nullify the effects of damaging debuffs, such as from Poisoned or On Fire!, with the exception of Hunger. Life Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.

name: Life Crystal
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Life Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health capacity by 20, adding a red heart to the player's health bar, while also restoring 20 health. Life Crystals can be found naturally placed in any area in the Underground layer and below, though they are fairly uncommon. They cannot be found in the Underworld or the Dungeon. Life Crystals also have a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to drop from a Golden Crate, or 19/160 (11.88%) chance from a Titanium Crate. Up to 15 Life Crystals can be used per player, increasing health capacity by 300 health (15 hearts). Added to the 100 health (5 hearts) new players begin with, a total of 400 health (20 hearts) can be achieved. Additional Life Crystals can no longer be used at that point, and attempting to do so will not consume the item. After a world converts to Hardmode, and after the 400 health maximum is reached from consuming Life Crystals, Life Fruits can then be used to increase health capacity further, to a maximum of 500 health (20 Life Fruits).

name: Life Crystal Boulder
obtain: Crafted at a Heavy Assembler and Ecto Mist.
description: The Life Crystal Boulder is a furniture item. It spawns naturally in the Celebration Mk 10, No Traps, and the Zenith special world seeds. It appears to be an ordinary Life Crystal and is generated in a similar manner upon world creation, but acts identically to a Boulder if hit with a pickaxe or drill, or otherwise unsupported by solid blocks. The Life Crystal Boulder falls directly downwards until it collides with a solid block, at which point it begins rolling, accelerating and dealing damage to the player, enemies, critters, and NPCs. Life Crystal Boulders pierce through an unlimited number of entities and accelerate to a top speed of 36 mph over the course of 2.17 seconds. Life Crystal Boulders roll across flat surfaces and down slopes but break and disappear upon colliding with an obstacle, such as a wall of solid tiles. They deal 140 / 280 / 420 to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters) and inflict a knockback value of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact. However, when the Life Crystal Boulder breaks after colliding with solid blocks or after rolling for one minute (like all other projectiles), it drops a Life Crystal item.

name: Life Drain
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Life Drain is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. When used, it creates an invisible aura that deals continuous damage to all enemies near the cursor's position, as long as the line of sight between the player and the cursor is unobstructed. A stream of red particles flows toward the player from each targeted enemy. While the aura is hitting enemies, the user receives the Life Drain buff, which adds 1.5 health per second to existing health regeneration, plus 0.5 health per second for every two extra enemies hit, while also increasing the ramp-up speed of natural regeneration greatly. Enemies that are being damaged by the Life Drain's aura are additionally inflicted with a unique debuff that deals 25 damage per second. Its best modifier is Mythical for damage output, or Celestial for mana conservation.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Life Fruit is a Hardmode plant and permanent booster item that grows on Jungle grass in any area within the Underground layer or below, and only after any mechanical boss has been defeated. Life Fruit grow 25% faster on average in Expert Mode. When used, a Life Fruit permanently increases the player's health capacity by 5 and restores the player's health by 5, turning one unit in the player's health bar golden. Life Fruit can only be used once a player has reached the 400 health cap from consuming Life Crystals. A total of 20 Life Fruit is required to reach the maximum 500 health capacity. Once this is reached, the player's health cannot be increased beyond 500, with the exception of the Lifeforce buff.

name: Lifeforce Potion
description: The Lifeforce Potion is a buff potion that grants the Lifeforce buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's health capacity by up to 20% (see below for details). This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time by right-clicking the icon (), by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or by double-tapping the buff icon (). Maximum health granted by the Lifeforce buff will not be counted by health conditions of certain game mechanics (e.g. the spawning of Nurse, Eye of Cthulhu, and Goblin Army, etc.). The player have to increase their permanent maximum health (with permanent boosters) to fulfill these conditions.

description: The Light Disc is a Hardmode, post-The Destroyer boomerang. It does not necessarily return immediately upon contact with objects, but instead can bounce off blocks before returning. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with a maximum of six Light Discs that can be thrown out at one time. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

name: Light's Bane
description: The Light's Bane is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it creates a dark slash near the tip of the sword. The slashes deal 50% of the weapon's damage (8 base damage) and its full knockback, have 5 armor penetration, pierce once, and will automatically target enemies within a radius of 3.125 tiles. The weapon also has a chance to create a big slash that is twice as large and deals 100% of the weapon's damage. The chance of big slashes occurring is equal to the player's melee critical strike chance. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Blood Butcherer. The Light's Bane is faster than the Blood Butcherer, but has a lower size and base damage. Its best modifier is Legendary.

name: Lightning Boots
description: The Lightning Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory and the direct upgrade to the Spectre Boots. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint. Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second). The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail. When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time.

name: Lightning Bug
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Lightning Bug is a harmless Hardmode critter that gives off a tiny amount of light, similarly to the Firefly. It spawns on Hallowed grass blocks during the night. The Lightning Bug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Lightning Bug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Lightning Bug in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Lightning Bug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Lightning Bug can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power. The Lightning Bug can be spawned by the Firefly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. Its counterpart is the Firefly.

description: The Lightning Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Volt Bunny that follows the player. While flying to keep pace with the player, the Volt Bunny dashes and releases a series of spherical blue sparks, which emit a decent amount of light while moving erratically and can spread light over an area. If there are no available tiles for the pet to "sit" on, like when climbing walls or flying, the Volt Bunny will constantly jump around. The Lightning Carrot can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after completing 50% (273 entries) of the Bestiary.

name: Lightning Strike
description: The Lightning Strike is a Hardmode wand that is an upgrade to the Thunder Zapper. When used, it creates a blue marker which follows the cursor but is obstructed by blocks. If there is no line of sight between the player and the cursor during use, the marker will be created at the closest block in the direction of the cursor. After a short delay, lightning strikes the position of the marker, damaging any enemies in its path and inflicting the Hellfire debuff. When the blue marker is struck underwater, several shocks will be created in a large circle within the water, dealing damage to enemies and the player while inflicting the Zapped debuff for 4–7 seconds. If the initial marker intersects an enemy, it will lock onto the enemy, following it like a natural lightning strike in a Thunderstorm. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is instantly summoned. The Lihzahrd Altar is always found naturally placed in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple. Like Lihzahrd Bricks, the Lihzahrd Altar is impervious to explosions and can only be removed with the Picksaw, Laser Drill, or Luminite Pickaxes. Once picked up, it can be placed anywhere and can be used to summon Golem in any area at any time, as long as the world is in Hardmode with Plantera defeated.

description: The Magic Lantern is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a small glowing Magic Lantern which hovers above the player, emitting dim yellow light. The lantern will also highlight all treasure within up to 15 tiles from the lantern's location, overlaying small yellow sparkles over nearby valuable treasure, which is similar to the sparkling effect produced by a Spelunker Potion. The Magic Lantern can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 10 Gold during the night of a full moon. The lantern will always try to maintain a position just forward of and above the player, passing through blocks as needed. If the player is far enough away or in midair, the lantern will propel itself with a rocket exhaust in order to catch up to them. The lantern's position can block objects of interest at ceiling height, but if the player just turns around, the lantern will move to their other side.

description: The Magnet Sphere is a Hardmode, post-Plantera spell book that has a 1/300 (0.33%) / 599/90,000 (0.6656%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones in the post-Plantera Dungeon. When used, it fires a slow-moving cyan sphere that rapidly fires instantaneous, non-piercing beams at the closest enemy as it travels. It passes through all enemies and bounces off solid blocks. The sphere dissipates after 15 seconds have passed, it has traveled 52 tiles, or when another sphere is fired. Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Magnet Sphere's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.

When one of these stars strikes an obstacle, it will transform into a special glowing mana star that travels towards the player, restoring 50 mana upon collection. name: Mannequin
description: The Mannequin is a furniture item that can be used to display armor, weapons, and vanity items, as well as accessories and dyes. Items can be placed on a Mannequin by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are three slots for helmet, shirt, and pants, five slots for accessories, and one slot for weapons. In addition, each slot besides the weapons slot has an associated dye slot underneath it. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Mannequin. Mannequins can only be removed if no items are placed on them. The Mannequin always displays armor and clothing in their male sprite forms. The Womannequin can be used to display them in their female counterparts. The pose of a Mannequin can be changed by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on it whilst holding any hammer. This changes its appearance, as well as the position of the weapon that it is holding.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Meteorite is a pre-Hardmode ore typically mined from Meteorite crash sites. It also spawns in high numbers during a Meteor Shower and rarely drops from Meteor Heads. A Meteorite crash site is a mini-biome guaranteed to spawn after the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu is defeated for the first time. If the boss is defeated between midnight and dawn (12:00 AM – 4:30 AM), then the meteor crashes immediately. Otherwise, it will crash at the next midnight (12:00 AM). Meteorite can be mined using a Tungsten Pickaxe or better (its counterpart, the Silver Pickaxe, does not have enough pickaxe power). Contact with Meteorite blocks causes the player to be inflicted with the Burning debuff, unless the player has the Obsidian Skull accessory (or its upgrades) equipped, or is using an Obsidian Skin Potion.

name: Minecart Track
description: Minecart Tracks are placeable furniture-type blocks that allow for rapid transportation over long distances. They form a continuous track when placed next to each other, and form slopes when placed diagonally. Although they cannot be walked on, they can be grappled using a hook. Minecart Tracks generate in large quantities in Abandoned Minecart Tracks(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), but can also be obtained via crafting. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff ( right-clicking the icon, selecting the icon and canceling it in the equipment menu, double-tapping the icon, or canceling the buff from the buffs screen). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The player can alternatively move on top of Minecart Tracks using Roller Skates.

description: The Minecart Upgrade Kit is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses permanent booster item that permanently unlocks a boost for all Minecarts, including a speed increase, extra defense when moving, and a laser attack. It also drops a Mechanical Cart when used. The Minecart Upgrade Kit can only be obtained by combining the Mechanical Wheel Piece, Wagon Piece, and Battery Piece, which are dropped from the Treasure Bags of the mechanical bosses in Expert Mode. The Minecart boost can be toggled via a toggle on the Minecart slot in the equipment menu.

description: The Molotov Cocktail is a consumable ranged weapon with a relatively short throwing arc. Upon hitting a solid object or enemy, it will explode and release 6 Molotov Fire light emitting projectiles, which can hit up to 3 targets. These smaller projectiles deal 50% damage (11 base damage), apply no knockback and inflict the On Fire! debuff on enemies for 3–6 seconds. Its high damage and ability to inflict fire damage make it a powerful early- to mid-pre-Hardmode weapon.

name: Molten Charm
description: The Molten Charm is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that combines the effects of the Lava Charm and Obsidian Skull. When the Molten Charm is equipped and the player comes into contact with lava, a 7-second countdown begins, signified by a lava meter that displays over the player's head. It operates similarly to the Breath meter, but displays flame icons instead of bubbles. Lava immunity time is recharged gradually by exiting lava, the same way breathing time is recharged by exiting water (albeit much more slowly). The Molten Charm also grants immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted by contact with Meteorite, Hellstone, and Hellstone Brick. It does not grant immunity to other fire-based damage.

The floating Piggy Bank despawns after 3 minutes, but can be resummoned repeatedly at no cost. The Flying Piggy Bank does not follow the player like pets or minions would, instead it hovers stationarily at the point summoned. name: Moonglow
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: Moonglow is a type of herb which appears as a bent stalk with a drooping blue-white flower. It grows naturally on regular Jungle grass. Moonglow can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Moonglow Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Moonglow blooms during nighttime (7:30 PM to 4:29 AM). Its blooming is indicated by the blue flower and blue-white light particles emitted. Harvesting mature Moonglow yields 1 Moonglow item. Harvesting blooming Moonglow yields 1 Moonglow item and 1–3 Moonglow Seeds. Harvesting blooming Moonglow with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Moonglows and 1–5 Moonglow Seeds instead. Both Moonglow and Moonglow Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Mouse is a critter that spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, but not in Ice, Crimson, Corruption, Jungle or Hallow biomes. It can also spawn in front of unsafe Living Wood Walls below the surface at a much higher rate. Its small size and speed can make it difficult to spot even in well-lit conditions, although it occasionally squeaks. The Mouse has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players. The Mouse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Mouse Cage). Once crafted, the Mouse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Mouse can be spawned by the Mouse Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the Desktop version, Console version, and Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Mouse to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

description: Mushroom Grass Seeds are seeds that have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to drop from harvesting Glowing Mushrooms. The seeds can also be purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver 50 Copper each if she is spoken to in a Glowing Mushroom biome. Shaking a Giant Glowing Mushroom occasionally yields Mushroom Grass Seeds as well. They can also be obtained by using Poo on an Extractinator. Mushroom Grass Seeds must be planted on Mud Blocks and can be grown both above and under ground. Once planted, Mushroom grass will begin to spread to adjacent Mud Blocks and grow Glowing Mushrooms, as well as Giant Glowing Mushrooms when enough space is available. Mushroom grass spreads much slower than ordinary or Corrupt grass, at a speed comparable to Jungle grass – 3–5 tiles per day for each continuous section of Mud Blocks. Mushroom grass, as well as the mushrooms that grow on it, emit moderate light.
notes:
Mushroom Grass Seeds are seeds that have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to drop from harvesting Glowing Mushrooms. The seeds can also be purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver 50 Copper each if she is spoken to in a Glowing Mushroom biome. Shaking a Giant Glowing Mushroom occasionally yields Mushroom Grass Seeds as well. They can also be obtained by using Poo on an Extractinator.

description: The Musket is a pre-Hardmode gun. It will always drop from the first Shadow Orb destroyed in a Corruption world (along with 100 Musket Balls) and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Shadow Orbs afterward. It also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Corrupt(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) fished in the Corruption. The Musket has a base 12% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its Crimson counterpart is The Undertaker. The Musket deals a much higher damage per shot at a slower fire rate. Its best modifier is Unreal.

name: Musket Ball
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Musket Ball is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It has no special properties and is used for crafting a variety of more advanced ammunition. When either Musket Balls or Tungsten Bullets are fired with certain guns, they will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Uzi converting them into High Velocity Bullets). Some other guns, such as the Pew-matic Horn, can convert any type of bullet. Musket Balls can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 7 CC each, or 70 SC for 1000 rounds. They can also be obtained from Shadow Orbs and Crimson Hearts (along with a Musket or The Undertaker), or from a Present (along with a Red Ryder) during Christmas. The Endless Musket Pouch serves as an infinite amount of Musket Balls.

description: The Nail Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Nails as ammunition. When used, it fires a Nail that deals 15% of the weapon's damage (17 base damage) and sticks to enemies or blocks before exploding after 1.5 seconds, dealing 135% damage (155 base damage). Nails are unaffected by gravity until they have traveled roughly 30 tiles, after which they move with an arc similar to that of arrows. The Nail Gun has a 1/25 (4%) / 49/625 (7.84%) chance of being dropped by Nailheads during the Solar Eclipse event. The Nail Gun is always dropped alongside 100–200 Nails. Additional Nails are also sold by both the Merchant and the Arms Dealer for 1 Silver each when the player has the Nail Gun in their inventory. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

name: Nano Bullet
description: The Nano Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bullet. It inflicts the Confused debuff on hit for 1–3 seconds, reversing enemy movement to make them run away from the player rather than towards them. The fired Nano Bullets receive a 1.25× damage multiplier, which is applied to the total damage of gun and bullet, and after other damage bonuses. Nano Bullets can also bounce off blocks once, disippating upon hitting blocks for the second time. They bounce towards the direction of the nearest enemy within a 50-tile radius that has an unobstructed line of sight of to the bullet, but will only deal 66% damage after bouncing. Nano Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Nano Bullets is 17 Silver 50 Copper, which is 35 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Nano Bullets is 35 Gold.

name: Nebula Arcanum
description: The Nebula Arcanum is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist magic weapon that fires a swirling purple orb when used. The orb will slowly home in on enemies within a 50-tile range and bounce off blocks, hitting three times before exploding into 10–16 smaller shard projectiles that each deal 65% of the weapon's listed damage (45 base damage), inflict 80% of its knockback (base knockback of 4 (Weak)), and do not pierce. All three hits do not have to be on the same target, as it will continue to home in on other enemies in range if its target dies before the third hit. If the projectile does not hit enemies three times, it will explode after 11 seconds. As the main orb remains active, it also produces additional, smaller orb projectiles that orbit around it, each of which deals 50% of the weapon's listed damage (35 base damage), passes through blocks, inflicts no knockback, and pierces an unlimited number of enemies. A maximum of eight of these projectiles can be summoned per orb. Two to three of these projectiles appear per second for the first half of the projectile's lifetime and disappear at the same rate as it approaches its detonation. Its best modifier is Mythical.

obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Nimbus Rod is a Hardmode magic weapon that creates storm clouds that drop damaging "rain" projectiles directly below themselves. When cast, a cloud projectile is fired from the Nimbus Rod and travels towards the cursor. Upon reaching its destination or colliding with a solid block, the cloud stops and starts sending damaging raindrop particles downward, each dealing the weapon's stated damage. The raindrop can hit up to 5 targets. Each cloud lasts for five minutes and up to two clouds can be spawned at once. Using the Nimbus Rod when there are already two active clouds will cause the oldest cloud to disappear. The Nimbus Rod has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Angry Nimbuses. Its best modifier is Demonic because it cannot get modifiers that affect knockback.

name: Oasis
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Oasis is a naturally spawning mini-biome that can be found on the Surface layer of the Desert biome. It consists of a sizable body of water surrounded by multiple palm trees and shrubbery such as mini cacti, ferns, and flowers. Cattail plants grow in the lake and there are often multiple Dragonflies flying around and above the surface of the water. The water of the Oasis is a turquoise color, just like that of regular surface Desert water. An Oasis Water Fountain can be purchased in order to replicate this water color at a location of choice. As a mini-biome, the Oasis is not considered to be a separate biome from the Desert: the Oasis counts as a Desert in terms of an NPC's preferred biome, the Oasis will spawn Desert-exclusive critters and enemies, and fishing in an Oasis will yield the same results as fishing in a Desert. Thus, it is possible to create an artificial Oasis by placing water in the surface layer of a Desert biome.

name: Owl
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Owl is a critter that spawns near Towns on the surface Forest and Hallow during the night, when it is not raining. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest tree at night. The Owl has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Owl can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Owl Cage). Once crafted, the Owl cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Owl can be spawned by the Owl Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

The Owl is a critter that spawns near Towns on the surface Forest and Hallow during the night, when it is not raining. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest tree at night. The Owl has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players.
The Owl can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Owl Cage). Once crafted, the Owl cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.
The Owl can be spawned by the Owl Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

description: The Paladin's Hammer is a Hardmode, post-Plantera boomerang that has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 29/225 (12.89%) chance of being dropped by Paladins in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it swings in a similar manner to a broadsword before being thrown at a high velocity that deals 33% increased damage on the first hit. The thrown hammer can pierce an infinite number of enemies, but loses 10% damage on each hit and returns to the player after traveling a long distance or upon hitting solid blocks. Both the hammer and its explosion inflict the Broken Armor debuff for 1.5 seconds, which adds 20 armor penetration against enemies and halves defense of players. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

name: Peace Candle
description: The Peace Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light and can be placed only on flat-surface items. When placed or held, it gives nearby players the Peace Candle buff. The Peace Candle buff decreases spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%. The buff is applied to any players holding a Peace Candle or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Peace Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Multiple Candles will not stack with each other, even if one is placed and the other held. Peace Candles can only be placed on platforms and flat furniture items like Work Benches and Tables. The Peace Candle can be made from a Pink Torch and either Gold Bars or Platinum Bars, meaning that the player needs to have defeated Pinky at least once to craft this item. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on Peace Candles shuts them off, and they will toggle when activated via wiring. Peace Candles that are turned off will not activate the Peace Candle buff. The Peace Candle's effect is the opposite of the Water Candle, which increases enemy spawn rate. If a Peace Candle and a Water Candle are active at the same time, they will cancel each other's effects out, resulting in no difference in spawn rate.

name: Pearlstone Block
description: The Pearlstone Block is a Hardmode block type found in The Hallow. It requires at least a Nightmare Pickaxe, Deathbringer Pickaxe, or explosives to mine. Pearlstone is the Hallow version of Stone (similar to Ebonstone in The Corruption, or Crimstone in The Crimson). In a way similar to Ebonstone and Crimstone, Pearlstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Vile Powder, Vicious Powder, or the Clentaminator with the Green Solution. During the initial creation of the Hallow biome upon the defeat of the Wall of Flesh, Stone blocks in the conversion path become Pearlstone blocks (see Hardmode). Pearlstone itself also continues to spread Hallow to all Stone, Sand, Ice, and Grass covered dirt within a three tile radius. Over time, it will grow Crystal Shards if it is in the Cavern layer or below.

name: Penguin
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Penguin is a harmless critter that only spawns in the Snow biome and may spawn with different colors. The Penguin has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Penguin can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Penguin Cage). Once crafted, the Penguin cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Penguin can be spawned by the Penguin Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile/Vicious Powder, Penguins will turn into Corrupt Penguins or Vicious Penguins.

name: Phantasm
description: The Phantasm is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist bow. When used, it fires a burst of four arrows that are loosely grouped together, while only consuming one arrow per use. Its fire rate will gradually increase while in use. Upon enemy hits, the Phantasm fires an additional burst of three Phantasm Arrow projectiles. Phantasm Arrows home in on the hit target, move through blocks, deal 30% of the original projectile's damage, and inflict no knockback. The Phantasm has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance of not consuming ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.

name: Phantom Phoenix
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Phantom Phoenix is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss bow. When used, it fires a slight spread of two arrows, alongside a large Phoenix projectile on every third use. The weapon only consumes 1 arrow per use, and its use time is increased by 50% after firing a Phoenix projectile (base use time of 27 (Average)) but returns to normal after firing arrows. The Phoenix projectile deals 200% of the weapon's damage (74 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) and 100% of its knockback (base knockback of 4 (Weak) when using Wooden Arrows), inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 8 seconds and pierces infinitely, but loses 5% of its damage per hit. The Phoenix explodes after traveling for 2 seconds or upon colliding with blocks and liquids, dealing damage within a 6×6-tile rectangular area centered around the point of impact. The Phantom Phoenix also converts Wooden Arrows into Flaming Arrows, without increasing their damage. The Phantom Phoenix is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Its best modifier is Unreal.

description: The Piece of Moon Squid is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pet-summoning item that spawns a Moonling, which resembles the Moon Lord's head, that follows the player. The Piece of Moon Squid has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord in Master Mode.

name: Piggy Bank
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Piggy Bank is a portable storage item which can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 GC. It requires a flat-surface item for placement. It has 40 slots like other storage items. The Piggy Bank inventory can also be accessed via the Money Trough(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Eye Bone(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Unlike normal Chests, the Piggy bank (along with the Safe, Defender's Forge, and Void Vault) is considered "personal storage". Items contained in a Piggy Bank are attached to the character rather than to a container in the world: The bank can be picked up and moved regardless of the items within. Coins and items stored within it are safe from other players, and will not be dropped on death. They will even travel with a character who goes to a different world. However, if a Hardcore character dies, all items in their personal storage will be deleted with the character and permanently lost.

name: Pink Horseshoe Balloon
description: The Pink Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, grants a double jump, and grants +0.05 luck. The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double jump's height is increased from 7 blocks to 13 blocks, reaching a total of 23.5 blocks with both jumps. Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 17.5 blocks (8 blocks + 9½ blocks from Tsunami jump) to 15 blocks (7 blocks + 8 blocks from Tsunami jump).

name: Piranha Gun
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Piranha Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged weapon that costs no ammunition. It fires a spread of three returning Mechanical Piranha projectiles that inflict the Hemorrhage debuff for 4-6 seconds on hit. The Mechanical Piranha initially moves in a straight path until it collides with an enemy, at which point it latches into the target, follows its movement and deals continuous damage while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held. If the initial target is killed and the button is still held, the projectiles will home in towards other nearby enemies. The Piranhas return to the gun when the button is released or once no other enemies are in the vicinity, and despawn after one minute of continuous use. Any Piranhas that return to the gun while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held will be automatically relaunched towards the cursor. Each Piranha can target different enemies, or the same one if there are too few nearby. The Piranha Gun is always found in the Dungeon's Jungle Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Jungle Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Unreal. Because its attack speed is unaffected by modifiers, Godly and Demonic can also be considered the best modifiers for the Piranha Gun.

name: Pixel Box
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Pixel Box is a mechanism that can be bought from the Mechanic for 2 Silver. When activated, it looks fully illuminated but does not emit light. Pixel Boxes can be placed anywhere, even if a wall is not present, similarly to Logic Gates. They are always placed in the deactivated state. If a wire below or above the Pixel Box is turned on at the same time as a wire to the left or right of the Pixel Box, it will turn on. Turning on the wire only below or above or only to the left or right will have no effect. Wires must be placed on the Pixel Box in order for them to function.

name: Poo
description: Poo is a type of decorative block obtained by sitting on a toilet while any tier of the Well Fed buff is active. The time until Poo is produced is random, though it averages to 10 seconds. Having the Tipsy debuff will reduce this time by 66.67%. Producing Poo will remove the food buff, and the number of blocks dropped increases with the type of the buff and its remaining duration. The maximum number of Poo blocks acquirable at once is 169, from a Golden Delight with 47 minutes of buff time remaining while the player has negative luck. When Poo is placed down, small flies will continuously fade in and out around it as a visual effect. The quantity of flies scales with the amount of Poo blocks placed in one area. Additionally, Poo blocks apply 3 seconds of the Stinky debuff to all players standing on them. Poo blocks create a squelchy sound when stepped on, and landing on top of them will also not inflict fall damage. Poo can also generate naturally in Truck stop worlds or drop from the Jungle Mimic in Celebration Mk 10 worlds. Poo can be used on an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to obtain Dirt, Grass Seeds, Jungle Grass Seeds, and Mushroom Grass Seeds.

name: Portal Gun
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Portal Gun is a Hardmode tool that is always dropped from the Moon Lord. It launches projectiles that create up to two different portals upon contact with blocks: one fired using ⚒ Use / Attack, the other using ⚷ Open / Activate. Any player or NPC that touches one portal will be instantly transported to the other one, without losing momentum. Enemies, critters, projectiles, items, or liquids cannot be teleported. While selected, the Portal Gun will also alter the player's physics: their maximum fall speed is multiplied by 3.5 (from 51 mph to 179 mph) and horizontal momentum/inertia is kept while in the air. This effect is also applied if the last entity that affected the player's fall was a portal. The Cyborg sells the Portal Gun Station if the player has a Portal Gun in their inventory when speaking to him. On the We don't even test for that secret world seed, the Portal Gun has a 1/7 (14.29%) of being obtained from any Chest.

The Cyborg sells the Portal Gun Station if the player has a Portal Gun in their inventory when speaking to him.

name: Portal Gun Station
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Portal Gun Station is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord furniture item and mechanism that can fire portals, similar to the Portal Gun. The Portal Gun Station can be purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold if the player has a Portal Gun or another Portal Gun Station in their inventory. Once placed, pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on different spots on the Portal Gun Station triggers different effects: pressing at the top toggles between orange and blue portal colors; pressing at the base fires a portal; pressing at the left or right side rotates its shooting direction. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, each rotation tilts it by one step (22.5°). The Portal Gun Station can also be triggered by wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either change portal color, shoot portal (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds), or rotate toward the side the wire is on. Only a pair of portals can exist at a time for each player that has the Portal Gun or Portal Gun Station, whether created by the former or the latter.

description: The Psycho Knife is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Psychos during the Solar Eclipse event. When holding the Psycho Knife and standing still, the player will quickly enter stealth, causing them to turn almost invisible, move much more slowly, and no longer be targeted by certain enemies' projectile attacks. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 0.83 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values: +300% melee damage (increases the weapon's damage to 340 without additional melee bonuses) +30% melee critical strike chance (34% base chance) +100% melee knockback (7 (Strong) base knockback) −750 aggro −50% movement speed; then sets sprint speed equal to move speed As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details). Stealth mode additionally prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using items. Stealth mode is deactivated upon hitting an target, switching to a different item, riding a mount, or taking damage. Swinging the weapon alone does not cancel stealth, nor does moving. However, moving or swinging the weapon before stealth mode is fully engaged will quickly deactivate stealth. Its best modifier is Legendary. Due to rounding, the Light modifier gives the same speed bonus as Legendary, with fewer other bonuses.

name: Rainbow Boulder
description: The Rainbow Boulder is a rare object that can be encountered in Boulder traps, where it occasionally replaces the regular Boulder. It can be found more commonly in Celebration Mk 10 worlds. It looks like a light gray bumpy stone with a rainbow glow behind it, and is accompanied with colored sparkles in front of it, although they do not illuminate light. Like normal Boulders, the Rainbow Boulder starts to move when it is unsupported (e.g. when the pressure plate wired to the trap is activated) or when it is struck with a pickaxe or drill. It does not drop and roll sideways, however. Instead, it starts flying across the screen, emitting light as it does this, traversing through blocks, and attacking nearby enemies, dealing high damage. It also targets treasures, similar to fairies, and leaves sparkles at its location. It moves around for approximately one minute. During this time, a unique music track also plays. The Rainbow Boulder can be crafted and placed by the player. Player-placed Rainbow Boulders have the same behavior as naturally generated ones when activated.

name: Rainbow Brick
description: Rainbow Brick is a Hardmode brick that can be obtained as a drop from the Rainbow Slime. It glows in the dark when placed, and cycles through the colors of the rainbow. The cycling colors of Rainbow Bricks, Rainbow Brick Walls, Helium Moss, Helium Moss Brick, Helium Moss Brick Walls, Rainbow Torches, the Disco Ball, and Rainbow Hair Dye are synchronized with each other. If a waterfall passes through a Rainbow Brick, it will also cycle through the colors. Rainbow Bricks will not change the color of lavafalls, honeyfalls, or Shimmerfalls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

name: Rainbow Crystal Staff
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Rainbow Crystal Staff is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord summon weapon that summons a Rainbow Crystal sentry. It fires spreads of three multicolored light beams towards enemies, but cannot target through blocks. Each beam releases a star that explodes shortly after. Unlike most sentries, the Rainbow Crystal floats midair. The Rainbow Crystal Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 98.5% (including whip bonuses) or 24% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.

name: Rainbow Gun
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Rainbow Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic gun that fires a curving rainbow that persists for 40 seconds or until another rainbow is fired. Enemies touching the rainbow take damage repeatedly, approximately five times per second. The Rainbow Gun is always found in the Dungeon's Hallowed Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Hallowed Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Rainbow Gun's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.

name: Rainbow Rod
description: The Rainbow Rod is a Hardmode, post-The Twins wand. When used, it fires a rainbow missile that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the missile will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the missile homes in on nearby enemies and can pierce twice, creating a small explosion upon contact with a block or third enemy. The missile does not dissipate when touching a block while being controlled, and is not affected by liquids (unlike the Flamelash). Its best modifier is Mythical.

name: Ram Rune
obtain: Obtained through world generation, enemy drops, fishing, or purchase from NPCs.
description: The Ram Rune is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron accessory that can be obtained as secondary loot from Locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon, and from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. When equipped, it allows the player to do a "ground pound" by holding ▼ Down and pressing ↷ Jump while in midair. Pounding the ground creates a shockwave that deals 30 damage and knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to all enemies within 8 tiles of the player. If the player does the ground pound from a height of 10 tiles or more, the shockwave becomes empowered and instead deals a critical strike that inflicts 60 damage and knockback of 24 (Insane) to all enemies within 11 tiles of the player. Additionally, if the player makes direct contact with an enemy during the ground pound, the enemy will take an extra 40 damage as well as knockback of 5 (Average), and the player is granted 0.1 seconds of invincibility frames. This direct hit cannot critically strike.
